We introduce a conditional flow-matching model that estimates the reliability of single-gene effects from training-only cross-fitting and uses those estimates to calibrate the additive source distribution. The velocity is decomposed into a known correction of the additive reference and a learned residual transport field. On Norman genetic perturbations, reduces mean absolute error (MAE) from 0.142 to 0.131 for unseen combinations of observed singles and from 0.198 to 0.178 when constituent singles are withheld. On held-out ComboSciPlex drug combinations, MAE decreases from 0.191 to 0.176. Non-additive residual correlation improves from 0.574 to 0.638, and component ablations identify the contribution of reliability weighting. The results indicate that accounting for uncertain constituent effects improves generalization to unseen genetic and chemical combinations, with a moderate increase in training cost.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Kinetic Langevin Splitting Schemes for Constrained Sampling
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Constrained sampling, the task of generating samples from a distribution restricted to a convex set, is an important problem in computational statistics. In this paper, we propose new unadjusted sampling algorithms obtained by applying the symmetric BAOAB and ABOBA splittings, of the kinetic Langevin dynamics, to a penalized surrogate of the constrained target. This also includes their stochastic gradient versions. Since the Hessian of the penalized surrogate is discontinuous across the boundary of the constraint set, analyses relying on a Lipschitz Hessian do not apply. We therefore develop an analysis based only on strong convexity and smoothness, proving one-step Wasserstein contraction schemes, non-asymptotic Wasserstein bounds of both schemes and complexity bounds. The resulting complexities for the stochastic gradient versions improve substantially on traditional Euler-type discretizations. Numerical experiments verify our theory, which is tested on a toy problem and Bayesian constrained regression problem. Overall, the splitting schemes demonstrate stability at step sizes several times larger than Euler-type methods, require five to seventeen times fewer gradient evaluations for a given accuracy.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Optimal Deep Nonparametric Regression with Uniformly Bounded Lipschitz Constants
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Stability under input perturbations is necessary for deep neural network estimators in many applications involving noisy covariates or estimated features. Weight norm constraints are widely used to control sensitivity to input perturbations by bounding the Lipschitz constant of neural networks. However, existing approximation results under fixed bounds on standard norm products are insufficient to establish optimal statistical rates. In this paper, we establish a sharp approximation theory for deep ReLU networks under a split spectral norm product constraint. This theoretical result shows that sufficiently smooth Hölder functions can be uniformly approximated to arbitrary accuracy as the network depth increases, with the norm-product bound held fixed. We then propose a penalized least squares estimator for deep nonparametric regression. The resulting estimator has a uniformly bounded Lipschitz constant while still achieving the optimal nonparametric rate up to a logarithmic factor. As applications, we establish optimal prediction rates for two-stage learning and provide robustness guarantees under adversarial input perturbations. Numerical studies show that the penalized estimator has well-controlled sensitivity to input perturbations and prediction accuracy comparable to that of classical deep network methods.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Variance-Adaptive Upper Confidence Bounds for Multi-Armed Bandits with Kaplan--Meier Survival Estimation
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We study the stochastic multi-armed bandit problem in which the reward associated with each arm is the survival probability at a pre-specified time horizon, and the observed outcome is a right-censored time-to-event variable. Standard bandit algorithms face delayed and partial observations in this setting. Prior adaptations for the Kaplan--Meier (KM) estimator rely on Hoeffding-type bounds that ignore the inherent heteroscedasticity of continuous survival processes. To bridge this gap, we propose KM-UCB, a variance-adaptive policy that unites continuous-time survival analysis with discrete sequential decision-making. By leveraging martingale theory and continuous influence functions, we derive a fixed-cohort empirical Bernstein bound parameterized by Greenwood's variance formula. For realtime allocation, we retain the Greenwood index and use a survival bound from completed records to review the recommended arm. Under catch-up reporting, the policy has logarithmic expected regret with an arm-specific variance term in the exploration bound. We evaluate the original policy in a dual-layer delayed simulation and a retrospective replay of breast cancer trial data, and evaluate the correction in a separate paired simulation.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Risk-Controlled Correction for Frozen Multimodal Models under Missing Modalities
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: A deployed multimodal predictor may face missing modalities after its weights can no longer be changed. This raises a question that training-time repair does not answer: what part of the resulting error is still correctable from the information that remains? We show that this part is characterized by the Bayes gap, the difference between the model's prediction and the Bayes prediction given the observed modalities. For cross-entropy and squared error, excess risk measures this gap in the geometry of the loss; ambiguity in the observed modalities cannot be removed. Thus, a badly degraded prediction is not necessarily a correctable one. Estimating the Bayes prediction normally requires labels. However, when a model observing more modalities is conditionally correct, averaging its outputs conditional on the remaining modalities recovers this target without retrieval labels; with the same fixed blend and neighbors, it is no worse in expected cross-entropy or Brier risk than averaging hard labels. Some such assumption is unavoidable: otherwise the target is not identifiable from unlabeled data alone. GUARD (Gated Utility-Aware Recalibration for Deployment) leaves the deployed predictor unchanged. It estimates a candidate correction by retrieval, learns from deployment-matched labeled data when correction is likely to help, and calibrates a threshold on a held-out split by conformal risk control. Under exchangeability, the marginal probability that GUARD applies a correction whose loss increase exceeds a prescribed tolerance is bounded by a preset level, regardless of the learned score. In controlled experiments, correction gain follows headroom rather than raw error; across nine frozen model-dataset pairs spanning six domains, GUARD retains most of blanket correction's gain within harm budgets that blanket correction often exceeds.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. Under the mild assumption that the true distribution has a finite fourth moment, we further establish a uniform finite-sample performance guarantee for the proposed model. An iteratively reweighted majorization-minimization algorithm is also developed to solve the resulting nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problem, with a rigorous analysis of its convergence properties. Numerical experiments substantiate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and the practical effectiveness of the infinity-Wasserstein model in downstream applications.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Bad Genius: Counterfactual-Guided Harness Evolution Beyond Task-Specific Shortcuts
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: An optimized agent harness can improve on held-out tasks by relying on formatting conventions that those tasks share with the rest of the benchmark. We introduce Counterfactual Harness Search and Evolution (CHASE) to test whether harness improvements survive changes to the evaluation protocol. A Proposer edits the harness around a fixed foundation model. A Challenger then searches for a protocol change that preserves the tasks but reduces the updated harness's gain over the initial harness. Executable checks test whether the transformation preserves task semantics. If the gain loss is confirmed on held-out tasks, CHASE adds the transformation to an archive that constrains subsequent harness updates. We give conditions under which this finite archive bounds the gain loss on an ideal benchmark with shortcuts removed. We evaluate CHASE on Syn-Ledger, OfficeQA, FinanceBench, and SWE-Bench Pro V2. On Syn-Ledger, removing the known shortcuts yields 38.30% accuracy for CHASE and 18.27% for HarnessEvolve. On the 21 certification tasks from SWE-Bench Pro V2 HARD-51, changing the issue formatting and tool-output field order reduces HarnessEvolve's gain over the initial harness from 8.57 to 3.81 percentage points. The final CHASE harness retains 10.48 points of its 11.43-point gain under the same change.
Statistical Machine Learning.comment: 42 pages, 6 figures, including references and supplementary material

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Signature-Kernel Based Evaluation Metrics for Robust Probabilistic and Tail-Event Forecasting
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Standard sample-based metrics like Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) and Quantile Loss (QL) are frequently used in the evaluation of probabilistic time-series forecasting. However, these metrics fail to capture multivariate correlations or assess the ability to capture distribution tails. These global metrics are insensitive to errors on high-utility events in distributional tails due to over-representation of the distribution's body. To accurately measure distributional fidelity on tail-regions and regions of high utility while still having a proper scoring rule, we introduce a family of censored signature kernel metrics. Our proposed metrics concentrate evaluation of forecasts to a focus region, representing high-utility or distributional tails, by collapsing the body of the distribution to a single pivot. Our benchmarks on time-series foundation models (TSFMs) reveal that while a clear ranking can be formed for distribution capture, there is no clear winner for tasks like systemic load prediction. This indicates that models with a strong ability to capture an overall distribution do not produce forecasts with high downstream utility. To encourage the use of the proposed metrics we open-source the efficient signature kernel (ESK) library. This library facilitates batch computation, with custom triton kernels, achieving a speed-up of up to 3.58$\times$ compared to implementations via the popular SigKernel library. Code for our metrics are available on GitHub.
Statistical Machine Learning.comment: Accepted as a poster at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations and Datasets Track) Main Paper: 10 pages 2 figures Including Appendix and References: 19 pages 7 figures

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We give a complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties. We show that the determinantal equations arising from rank constraints imposed by the activation patterns generate the defining ideals, thereby proving a conjecture of Alexandr-Montúfar. The set-theoretic proof uses a characterization of orbit closures of matrix pencils in terms of the Kronecker canonical form.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Improved Leverage Score Sampling for Constrained Active Linear Regression
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: In this paper we study active learning for constrained linear regression. Given a design matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, a constraint set $C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, and query access to $b\in\mathbb{R}^n$, we seek an approximate solution to $\min_{x\in C}\|Ax-b\|_2^2$ using as few queries as possible. This problem arises in many scientific and engineering applications, and randomized leverage score sampling provides a powerful method to solve it. However, existing leverage score methods ignore the constraint or encode it through ridge regularization, suffering unfavorable query complexity for anisotropic constraint sets. We propose ellipsoid-regularized leverage scores, where we approximate the constraint set by an outer ellipsoid and use its shape matrix to bias sampling toward directions that matter under the constraint geometry. We prove that the query complexity is governed by an anisotropic effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}}(C)\le d$. With appropriate parameters, $O(d_{\text{eff}}(C)\log d/\varepsilon^2)$ queries suffice to return a point in $C$ with objective value at most $(1+\varepsilon)$ times the optimum. This bound can substantially improve on the standard leverage-score bound, since anisotropic constraints can make $d_{\text{eff}}(C)$ much smaller than $d$. For convex constraints, we improve the dependence on $\varepsilon$ from $1/\varepsilon^2$ to $1/\varepsilon$. We also prove two lower bounds: first, the $d/\varepsilon^2$ dependence is unavoidable without convexity assumptions on $C$, and second, in some regimes, the effective dimension dependence $d_{\mathrm{eff}}(C)/\varepsilon$ is necessary for ellipsoidal constraints. Experiments on synthetic regression problems and a parametric heat conduction problem show lower regression error than standard baselines for similar query budget.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Risk-optimal active learning with informative abstention
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We study label acquisition when an oracle may abstain and its response probability shares parameters with the classifier. A query can then provide information through both a returned label and the response outcome. Under a correctly specified parametric model, we derive the classifier information after adjustment for response-model nuisance parameters. Combining this information with the local curvature of multiclass zero-one risk gives an acquisition criterion for minimizing the leading asymptotic excess risk. We characterize the optimal allocation under a fixed query budget and show how query allocation affects response identifiability. The oracle criterion reduces to response-discounted acquisition when response probability does not depend on the classifier parameters. Simulations examine the resulting query allocations and isolate the contribution of the response-outcome term through an ablation. A Consumer Complaints replay retains observed human abstentions and reveals benchmark labels upon response. Response-aware acquisition has lower mean test error than response-discounted acquisition at the two largest budgets, with paired differences significant after Holm correction. Entropy sampling performs better at the smallest budget. The gains depend on the response mechanism and query budget.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We study smooth calibration error in sequential binary prediction, a measure of how far probabilistic forecasts are from being calibrated that is robust to small perturbations of the forecasts. The minimax smooth calibration error is known to lie between $Ω(T^{1/3})$ and $O(\sqrt T)$(Qiao and Zheng, 2024), where $T$ is the number of rounds. We close this gap for both adaptive and oblivious adversaries. We construct an adaptive adversary whose outcome mean moves with the forecaster's cumulative residual, which makes compensating for past residuals costly and forces every forecaster to incur $Ω(\sqrt T)$ expected smooth calibration error. Simulating this adversary against the forecaster's average prediction yields an oblivious adversary with the same guarantee. These lower bounds match the known $O(\sqrt T)$ upper bound up to universal constants, and are therefore minimax optimal. Our results also imply matching $Θ(\sqrt T)$ bounds for calibration distance and lower calibration distance. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Variable Length Diffuse Everything: Arbitrary Length Generative Modeling on Arbitrary State Spaces
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Diffusion and flow-based generative models have achieved remarkable results across diverse applications, but most assume data of fixed-dimension/length. Meanwhile, real-world problems such as layout generation often involve variable-length, multimodal data, such as continuous bounding box coordinates paired with discrete types. Existing methods typically address variable length by padding data to a fixed size or by introducing specialized objectives to model lengths explicitly, adding complexity and limiting generality. We propose Variable Length Diffuse Everything (VL-DE), a simple and general framework for variable-length multimodal generation on arbitrary state spaces. Instead of padding, VL-DE handles variable length through an insertion-based mechanism grounded in a principled theoretical framework, yielding a tractable training objective. In addition, by utilizing the fact that VL-DE is based on a generator with an additive form, we develop a higher-order sampler by appropriately handling the time dependence. Extensive experiments on layout and molecule generation demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: A Free Lunch: Gradient Averaging Achieves Optimal Statistical Efficiency in Newton Sketch
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We study statistical inference for online sketched Newton methods, in which each Newton system is approximately solved by an inner randomized sketching solver. Existing work reveals a computational--statistical trade-off: the sketching solver (and its accelerated variants) reduces the per-step cost of Newton methods from $O(d^3)$ to $O(d^2)$, but the randomness introduced by sketching also inflates the limiting covariance of both the last and the averaged Newton iterates. In this work, we address this trade-off via gradient averaging. We show that simply replacing the stochastic gradient with a moving average at each step can mitigate, and in some cases eliminate, the trade-off in Newton sketch. Importantly, gradient averaging requires no additional oracle evaluations and leaves the contraction bound of the inner sketching solver unchanged. In particular, we prove that the last sketched Newton iterate with gradient averaging attains a limiting covariance no larger than that without gradient averaging, while the averaged iterate even attains the minimax optimal limiting covariance, matching that of the exact Newton method. To our knowledge, this is the first analysis showing that randomness introduced to improve computational efficiency need not compromise statistical efficiency as long as proper gradient estimates are used. The key analytical challenge is that gradient averaging destroys the crucial martingale difference structure underlying central limit theorem arguments. We overcome this challenge by analyzing the coupled two-timescale recursions governing the iterate and the gradient estimator. Numerical experiments on linear and logistic regression support our theoretical covariance comparisons.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. Without access to labeled data, modern approaches typically employ self-supervised learning to obtain a model of normality. Since world models promise to build strong internal representations of their environment, we consider them as suitable candidates for the medical anomaly detection environment, namely medical investigations of healthy patients. To this end, we propose MADJEPA, a medical anomaly detector based on an enhanced multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). We design a multi-stage training pipeline to produce a robust detector: (1) image-based JEPA (I-JEPA) training aims to learn a strong representation of normal training data; (2) target encoder distillation aims to modulate over-generalization of I-JEPA representations to abnormal data; (3) pseudo-anomaly classification aims to calibrate anomaly predictions by learning a tight boundary around the normal data manifold. To demonstrate our design, we carry out comprehensive experiments on six datasets covering various medical image domains (e.g.~MRI, OCT, X-ray, histopathology), comparing our MADJEPA with numerous state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our carefully designed world model, MADJEPA, attains competitive results, ranking first on three datasets. Our ablation studies further confirm the utility of each training stage, indicating that I-JEPA alone is not sufficient to obtain competitive results in medical anomaly detection. We publicly release our code at https://github.com/Sabina085/madjepa.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted at WACV 2027

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Mammography Foundation Models for Opportunistic Prediction of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death among women, yet cardiovascular risk assessment often relies on clinical variables that may be missing, outdated, or unavailable in routine care. Screening mammography offers an opportunity for opportunistic cardiovascular risk stratification because it is routinely acquired and contains vascular features, including breast arterial calcifications (BAC), that are associated with cardiovascular risk and events. We evaluate whether mammography specific foundation models, originally pretrained for breast cancer related tasks, can transfer to cardiovascular risk prediction without cardiovascular specific supervision or explicit BAC annotation. We constructed a 5-year major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) cohort of 22,497 women linked to electronic health record outcomes, including 500 events (2.22% prevalence).Using only the screening mammogram, the foundation models achieved AUROCs of 0.823 and 0.822, recovering most of the gain of a clinical risk factor model (AUROC 0.859) over an age-only model (0.765), without requiring any clinical variables. Both foundation models evaluated assigned substantially higher predicted risk to patients with radiologist documented BAC, despite BAC never being used as a training label, and showed activation patterns consistent with vascular findings. Together, these findings suggest that mammography foundation models can recover clinically relevant cardiovascular risk information directly from mammographic pixels and suggest that screening mammography may provide an opportunistic source of cardiovascular risk information to complement conventional clinical assessment without additional imaging.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted at ML4H 2026

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Transferable Named Sparse Features for Morphology-based Gleason Grading
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Deep learning systems grade prostate biopsies at the level of pathologists, but most report a grade without the glandular architecture that justifies it. This work presents a grading system built on a sparse code over the tokens of a pathology foundation model. A sparse autoencoder pretrained on biopsies is aligned with multi-reader annotations, so that 69 of its 2048 features are named after Gleason morphologies such as cribriform glands, cords, and comedonecrosis. The same code feeds a grading network, which reads all features to predict Gleason patterns and the Grade Group, while morphology maps read directly from the named features. We evaluate the system on five public datasets that include needle biopsies, tissue-microarray cores, multi-reader annotations, and three scanners. The morphology maps remain stable across alignment runs and, without retraining, detect cribriform glands in external biopsies (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, 0.849) and pattern 5 in unseen cores when evaluated by up to six pathologists (AUROC 0.846 to 0.919). In an independent biopsy cohort, Grade Group agreement with three pathologists on Leica scans is close to their agreement with each other. Removing the named features reduces the corresponding Gleason pattern predictions by 49% to 98%, with effects larger than those from 20 activity-matched random feature removals. These results show that a shared sparse representation can support competitive Gleason grading while providing named morphological evidence that transfers across datasets and whose contribution to grading can be measured directly.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Single-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture. Users compare focal choices on one photograph, so content stability across edits matters alongside quality and speed. Recent generative methods rerun large diffusion models for every edit, even when they first restore an all-in-focus image, so content can change inconsistently between edits. Yet only this restoration is highly ill-posed and benefits from a generative prior, whereas rendering blur is largely determined by depth and the focal plane. We therefore propose FlashReFocus, which runs diffusion once per photograph and renders each edit with a lightweight network. A one-step diffusion deblurrer with a decoder refiner recovers fine detail efficiently while balancing fidelity and perceptual quality. The renderer uses an explicit defocus map for control and defocus-bias attention to promote information exchange between tokens with similar blur magnitudes. Because every edit reuses the same reconstruction, in-focus content stays consistent across edits, and editing the map enables tilt-shift and two-plane effects. We further collect 3CReal, a benchmark of 89 pairs from three camera-lens systems, to evaluate generalization to unseen optics. For zero-shot bokeh rendering on EBB! Val176 and 3CReal, FlashReFocus leads the evaluated methods in fidelity and perceptual quality. At 1536x1536, a complete refocus takes 2.45 s and each subsequent edit 0.46 s on one RTX PRO 6000.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 38 pages (8 main + appendix), 47 figures, 16 tables. Project page: https://ming053l.github.io/FlashReFocus/ Code: https://github.com/ming053l/FlashReFocus

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Joint Image Denoising and Interpolation via Mixed Graph Filtering
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Images often require both denoising and interpolation, yet treating the two tasks separately is suboptimal: interpolation introduces correlated noise that complicates subsequent denoising, while denoising may remove image details useful for interpolation. In this paper, we study joint image denoising and interpolation from a mixed graph filtering perspective, where denoising is modeled using undirected graph filters and interpolation using directed graph filters. We first establish that, under mild conditions, any (pseudo-)linear denoiser and interpolator can be interpreted as solution filters of maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problems regularized by undirected and directed graph smoothness priors, respectively. Guided by these results, we formulate graph-based joint denoising and interpolation problems using both directed and undirected graph structures. We characterize when joint denoising/interpolation reduces to a separable pipeline and when a genuinely coupled optimization is required. For the non-separable case, we recover sparse graph operators from given denoisers and interpolators, yielding an efficient linear-system formulation solvable via conjugate gradient. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed joint framework consistently outperforms separate denoising and interpolation pipelines across multiple denoiser-interpolator combinations.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Stochastic Optimisation for Scalable Ptychographic Image Reconstruction
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: X-ray ptychography is a lensless coherent diffraction imaging technique capable of high spatial resolution, in which an image is reconstructed by solving a large-scale inverse problem from highly redundant far-field diffraction measurements acquired under overlapping illumination. Whilst the measurement redundancy created by overlapping illumination is essential for reconstruction fidelity, it leads to computational and memory demands that scale poorly with object size and target resolution when using conventional reconstruction algorithms. This work proposes a ptychographic reconstruction framework that reduces peak memory usage and time to convergence by leveraging stochastic optimisation techniques developed for large-scale machine learning. Specifically, the framework employs stochastic gradient descent with a decaying step size that progressively reduces the effect of gradient noise, referred to here as variance reduction (VR), with gradients that agree with automatic differentiation, to optimise the ptychographic forward model using randomly sampled subsets of diffraction measurements. For an experimental dataset of 200,000 diffraction patterns of $128\times128$ pixels, VR is demonstrated to require $65\%$ of the peak GPU memory and $22\%$ of the reconstruction time of the established maximum-likelihood (ML) algorithm. The VR framework incorporates the Poisson maximum-likelihood formulation and partial coherence within a unified and extensible optimisation setting. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the framework achieves reconstruction quality visually comparable to established methods, with lower peak GPU memory and a shorter time
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 38 pages, 12 figures

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Micrograph B-factor estimation via Wilson statistics
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: The single-particle cryo-electron microscopy imaging process is known to cause exponential decay in the amplitude and power spectra of proteins. This decay is modeled by the B factor and is currently corrected as a post-processing stage of the 3D reconstruction. As a consequence, all experimental images in the dataset are assumed to share the same B factor. In this paper, we suggest a novel approach wherein the B factor is determined and corrected as a preprocessing step to the reconstruction. We show such an approach can improve reconstruction resolution.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Decoding Motion-Blurred QR Codes: Motion-Parameter Error Tolerance and Model-Based Recovery
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: In automated manufacturing, logistics, and inspection, Quick Response (QR) codes are often read on the fly under continuous ambient light without active strobes or motion pauses. The resulting relative three-dimensional motion produces spatially varying blur that defeats standard decoders, yet how accurately the motion must be estimated to recover the payload remains an open question. To address this question from a task-driven evaluation perspective centered on machine recognition effectiveness, we formulate motion-blurred QR recovery within a unified mathematical framework of identifiability. Within this framework, we systematically measure the decoding tolerance to perturbations in motion length, direction, rotation or scaling centre, and speed profile. These controlled experiments reveal three structural laws: 1) parameter tolerances shrink rapidly as blur amplitude grows and are tightest under uniform speed, whereas accelerating motion is substantially more forgiving; 2) length tolerance can differ markedly between underestimation and overestimation; 3) errors that are individually benign interact strongly and prevent decoding when combined. Guided by these findings, we propose a grey-box recovery pipeline in which two compact networks predict an initial corner trajectory, followed by tolerance-guided candidate search, alternating image-and-path fitting, and regularised linear inversion. On a benchmark of 955 real motion-blurred photographs spanning four camera models and four rigid-motion families, our method recovers the exact payload on 93.1% of the images. It outperforms the strongest fine-tuned deblurring network at 83.6% and reduces the decoding error rate by 58.0%, with zero wrong strings accepted.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Lifting 3D Gaussians: A Wavelet Multiresolution Representation for Scalable Gaussian Splatting Streaming
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) represents a scene as an unstructured set of primitives optimized at a single scale, offering no native support for progressive delivery to heterogeneous devices. Existing scalable approaches organize these primitives into independent quality layers or spatial hierarchies. However, maintaining separate splat representations across scales introduces redundancy, while independent layers have limited ability to correct coarse geometry as finer detail arrives. We present LiftGS, a multiresolution representation that organizes a scene into a coarse Gaussian set and a tree of refinements. Each refinement replaces one coarse Gaussian with two finer children whose attributes are learned relative to their parent. Inspired by wavelet lifting, we encode these changes using a shared detail vector and per-attribute factors that allow the two children to differ asymmetrically from the parent. A client first receives the coarse set, then reconstructs and substitutes children as refinement data arrives. This construction reuses previously transmitted attributes to encode finer detail and removes replaced parents from the active rendering set, reducing both refinement payload and rendering memory. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets show LiftGS cuts splat redundancy from over 65% to under 25%, reduces transmission payload and GPU memory by up to 2.4x and 5.5x over state-of-the-art scalable-3DGS baselines, achieves smooth quality transitions in simulated progressive delivery, and compresses a further 8.7x with standard coding at negligible quality loss. Project website: https://yuang-ian.github.io/liftgs/
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted by MMSys'27; Project page: https://yuang-ian.github.io/liftgs/

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Structure-Aware Sparse-View X-ray 3D Reconstruction
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: X-ray, known for its ability to reveal internal structures of objects, is expected to provide richer information for 3D reconstruction than visible light. Yet, existing neural radiance fields (NeRF) algorithms overlook this important nature of X-ray, leading to their limitations in capturing structural contents of imaged objects. In this paper, we propose a framework, Structure-Aware X-ray Neural Radiodensity Fields (SAX-NeRF), for sparse-view X-ray 3D reconstruction. Firstly, we design a Line Segment-based Transformer (Lineformer) as the backbone of SAX-NeRF. Linefomer captures internal structures of objects in 3D space by modeling the dependencies within each line segment of an X-ray. Secondly, we present a Masked Local-Global (MLG) ray sampling strategy to extract contextual and geometric information in 2D projection. Plus, we collect a larger-scale dataset X3D covering wider X-ray applications. Experiments on X3D show that SAX-NeRF surpasses previous NeRF-based methods by 12.56 and 2.49 dB on novel view synthesis and CT reconstruction. Code, models, and data are released at https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/SAX-NeRF . Our project page at https://caiyuanhao1998.github.io/project/SAX-NeRF/ shows more video and interactive results. An online Gradio demo is available on HuggingFace at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/SAX-NeRF
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: CVPR 2024; The first Transformer-based method for X-ray and CT 3D reconstruction

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Binarized Spectral Compressive Imaging
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Existing deep learning models for hyperspectral image (HSI) reconstruction achieve good performance but require powerful hardwares with enormous memory and computational resources. Consequently, these methods can hardly be deployed on resource-limited mobile devices. In this paper, we propose a novel method, Binarized Spectral-Redistribution Network (BiSRNet), for efficient and practical HSI restoration from compressed measurement in snapshot compressive imaging (SCI) systems. Firstly, we redesign a compact and easy-to-deploy base model to be binarized. Then we present the basic unit, Binarized Spectral-Redistribution Convolution (BiSR-Conv). BiSR-Conv can adaptively redistribute the HSI representations before binarizing activation and uses a scalable hyperbolic tangent function to closer approximate the Sign function in backpropagation. Based on our BiSR-Conv, we customize four binarized convolutional modules to address the dimension mismatch and propagate full-precision information throughout the whole network. Finally, our BiSRNet is derived by using the proposed techniques to binarize the base model. Comprehensive quantitative and qualitative experiments manifest that our proposed BiSRNet outperforms state-of-the-art binarization methods and achieves comparable performance with full-precision algorithms. Code and models are publicly available at https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/BiSCI and https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/MST . An online Gradio demo is available on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/MST
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: NeurIPS 2023; The first work to study binarized spectral compressive imaging reconstruction problem

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Words Speak Louder? Exploring the Language Shortcut of LLM-Driven Incomplete Multimodal Learning
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Is a face or a voice still heard once the words are known? Incomplete multimodal learning increasingly uses large language models (LLMs) as fusion engines: modality features enter as token blocks and missing modalities become placeholders. We find that LLM-driven fusion can override non-verbal evidence it can read. Contrasting its full-input prediction with counterfactual views, the same model shown one modality or no content, we identify language shortcuts. We build MR-Bench: MR-Bench-A types every test sample of four sentiment benchmarks; MR-Bench-H contains 900 human-validated clips (620 language-shortcut, LS; 280 non-verbal-shortcut, NS) from seven sources, and every model is scored on all of them. Zero-shot MLLMs solve at most 32.7% of the LS clips; adding the transcript to the muted video lowers vision-language accuracy by 46.1-53.1 points. Yet inverting a text-only model's answers solves 94.4%, so LS accuracy alone cannot establish use of non-verbal evidence. Inside the fusion LLM, fused states align increasingly with the text view late in the decoder. Counterfactual-View Reliability learning (CoVeR) trains views as unimodal judges and withholds fused supervision where they disagree. It achieves state-of-the-art results on five benchmarks without extra inference cost in accuracy mode. On MR-Bench-H, it reaches 61.7% LS and 93.6% NS accuracy; robust mode raises LS accuracy to 63.0% while lowering NS accuracy to 84.8%. Among LS clips solved without text, adding text causes errors on 30.1% with CoVeR versus 32.2% with LLM-Fusion. Project page: https://peacelwh.github.io/CoVeR/.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 14 tables. Project page: https://peacelwh.github.io/CoVeR/

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Coding agents make videos by writing and refining programs in a build--inspect--edit loop. A finished film costs a median of $2.85 in model calls and 11 minutes, over a third of that time in builds that block the agent. We find that much of this time is avoidable, for two reasons. First, 37.5% of the frames of a session's later films were drawn before, many shifted in time or inside an edited scene. Second, half of the builds stop at a check, where the agent needs only the verdict, but which builds stop is unknown until the checks finish. We present CodeReel, a training-free execution layer behind agents' existing commands. Exact frame reuse keys each frame by its drawing commands, regardless of its position in time, and reuses each frame whose key recurs. Blocking-aware scheduling runs the checks first and starts the render alongside them, at idle priority, unless the session's recent builds make a pass unlikely. Scheduling spends CPU to answer sooner and reuse returns it; exact keys let later versions use frames rendered for a failed one as the agent thinks. We introduce EditLoop, a benchmark of replayable agent sessions whose films are checked against renders from scratch. On it, CodeReel cuts the agent's wait by 36.3% against Rebuild, a warm pipeline with parallel rendering, and by 57.9% against Sequential, today's step-by-step pipeline. On time-shifting edits its reuse renders 43.9%, close to the 43.0% whose pixels are new, while Manim-style caching renders 99.8%. With real agents, the median wait per build is 0.62x Rebuild's in Claude Code, on topics never used in development, and 0.67x in Codex CLI. The gain holds for five models and two frameworks.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 19 pages, 8 figures, 14 tables

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: DAT: Dual-Aware Adaptive Transmission with Small-Large Model Collaboration for Edge-Cloud Anomaly Detection
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Continuous video anomaly detection is critical for timely safety monitoring in edge--cloud visual systems, but it remains challenging because abnormal events are sparse, transient, and require both low-latency anomaly detection and verifiable visual evidence. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer strong semantic understanding and visual reasoning capabilities for such event-centric analysis, yet applying them to continuous video streams incurs prohibitive computation and communication overhead under bandwidth-constrained edge--cloud deployments. To address this challenge, we propose DAT, a dual-aware adaptive transmission framework that supports high-quality semantic generation, low-latency anomaly detection, and progressive visual evidence supplementation. DAT first uses a collaborative small--large model cascade, where a lightweight edge-side model filters non-target-event frames, performs object detection, and triggers MLLM inference only for suspicious frames. Building on this cascade, DAT introduces visual guidance and semantic prompting to improve structured event understanding, localization, and output consistency. It further schedules semantic anomaly alarms and visual evidence through a semantic- and bandwidth-aware multi-stream transmission optimization method. Experimental results show that DAT achieves 97.77\% F1 in traffic-accident detection while substantially reducing inference and communication overhead. On continuous video workloads, DAT lowers the MLLM call rate to 13.71\% and reduces upload volume by at least 95.72\% compared with representative edge--cloud baselines. Under severe congestion, DAT reduces weighted alarm delay by up to 87.9\%, demonstrating efficient MLLM-based anomaly detection under constrained edge--cloud networks.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 9 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to AAAI 2027

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: AutoMV: An Automatic Multi-Agent System for Music Video Generation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Turning a full song into a music video (MV) requires interpreting its lyrics, which are often metaphorical, multilingual, and repeated across choruses, together with its musical character, and laying the resulting imagery out along the song's structure. Existing music-to-video systems produce short clips or audio-reactive visuals and make little use of lyric meaning. We present AutoMV, a training-free multi-agent framework in which LLM Screenwriter and Director agents plan a full-song visual narrative from time-aligned lyrics and music analysis, keep characters consistent through a shared character bank, and route each shot to cinematic or lip-sync rendering with verification. To evaluate full-song MVs, we build M2VBench: 30 released songs paired with their official MVs, objective audio--visual metrics, and a 12-criterion rubric rated by music-industry experts. Expert evaluation shows that AutoMV outperforms other baselines, although a gap remains to human-produced MVs. Ablation studies highlight the importance of time-aligned lyrics for musical theme alignment and storytelling. We further find that the selected multimodal judge, guided by our evaluation rubric, recovers the expert ranking of automatic systems, with some discrepancies in fine-grained assessments.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Relation-Aware Evidence Routing and Confidence-Guided Adaptation for Zero-Shot Visual Anomaly Detection
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Zero-shot visual anomaly detection (ZSAD) aims to identify and localize anomalies in unseen categories without target-domain adaptation, yet heterogeneous anomaly patterns and cross-domain variations challenge reliable detection. Existing approaches primarily rely on local visual features, patch-text similarities, or memory-based retrieval, leaving inter-patch relational information underexplored in anomaly evidence modeling. In this paper, we propose RACE-AD, a relation-aware evidence routing and confidence-guided adaptation framework that integrates local anomaly responses with attention-derived relational information for generalizable ZSAD. To capture inter-patch relationships, we characterize the dispersion of visual attention distributions using Shannon entropy, providing complementary relational statistics beyond local anomaly evidence. To organize heterogeneous evidence, we introduce relation-aware routing that combines memory-derived normal/anomaly responses with attention entropy to construct image-conditioned representations through entropy-regularized soft aggregation. To mitigate unreliable retrieval responses under domain shift, we design confidence-guided adaptation that regulates anomaly-conditioned representations according to the strength of the memory anomaly evidence and the relational dispersion before visual-semantic alignment. Extensive experiments on ten industrial and medical benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of RACE-AD, achieving average image-level AUROC and AP scores of 91.9% and 93.7%, and pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO scores of 93.6% and 80.0%, respectively. Ablation and diagnostic analyses show that entropy-guided routing mainly improves region-level localization and that the confidence gate is essential under domain shift.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Streaming Generative Video Compression with Embedding Alignment and In-Context Propagation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Video compression at ultra-low bitrates presents substantial challenges in preserving perceptual quality. Although pretrained video diffusion transformers (DiTs) provide powerful generative priors, existing generative video compression (GVC) methods built on them typically rely on computationally expensive VAE decoders to reconstruct video frames. Moreover, jointly refining multiple frames to exploit the inherent spatiotemporal modeling capabilities of video DiTs introduces additional buffering delay. To address these challenges, we propose SGVC, a streaming generative video compression framework that adapts a pretrained latent video DiT into a causal pixel-space refiner. Specifically, SGVC projects decoded features from a contextual pixel codec directly into the DiT input embedding space. To bridge the representation gap between codec-derived embeddings and pretrained DiT embeddings, we introduce Embedding Alignment, which aligns the projected embeddings with input embeddings extracted from the original frames during training. The refined DiT hidden states are then mapped directly to the pixel domain through a lightweight reconstruction path, bypassing the pretrained VAE decoder. To further exploit the spatiotemporal priors of the video DiT while maintaining causal decoding, we introduce In-Context Propagation, which reuses layer-wise K/V states across frames to exploit historical generative context, improving temporal consistency without requiring clip-wise buffering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SGVC achieves competitive rate-perception performance, with average BD-rate savings of 71.97% over S$^2$VC in terms of DISTS. Project Page: https://chigland.github.io/SGVC/
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 15 pages, 18 figures, 5 tables, including supplementary material

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Human-Data Interaction, Exploration, and Visualization Systems in the AI Era: Challenges and Opportunities
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: The rapid advancement of AI is transforming human-centered systems, with profound implications for human-AI interaction, human-data interaction, and visual analytics. In the AI era, data analysis increasingly involves large-scale, heterogeneous, and multimodal data that is predominantly unstructured, as well as foundation models such as LLMs and VLMs, which introduce additional uncertainty into analytical processes. These shifts expose persistent challenges for human-data interactive systems, including perceptually misaligned latency, scalability constraints, limitations of existing interaction and exploration paradigms, and growing uncertainty regarding the reliability and interpretability of AI-generated insights. Responding to these challenges requires moving beyond conventional efficiency and scalability metrics, redefining the roles of humans and machines in analytical workflows, and incorporating cognitive, perceptual, and design principles into every level of the human-data interaction stack. This paper investigates the challenges introduced by recent advances in AI and examines how these developments are reshaping the ways users engage with data, while outlining limitations and open research directions for building human-centered AI systems for interactive data analysis in the AI era.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: LeViT-UNet++: Towards Balanced Fine-Grained Details and Context for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Efficient medical image segmentation is essential for clinical applications requiring fast and accurate delineation, such as surgical navigation, radiation therapy, and real-time image-guided intervention. Despite substantial advances in convolutional neural networks and Transformers, attaining high accuracy under limited computational resources remains difficult, because reducing model complexity often sacrifices fine-grained structural details and global context modeling, yielding an unfavorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. To address this, we propose LeViT-UNet++, an efficient encoder-decoder architecture that better balances local detail preservation and global context modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Haar Wavelet Multi-Scale Downsampling (HWMD) module that decomposes feature representations into low- and high-frequency components to extract multi-scale structural information, thereby mitigating detail loss during downsampling. We further develop a depthwise convolution-based decoder that integrates multi-scale global representations from Transformer blocks with local spatial features, enabling progressive feature refinement while reducing computational overhead. Evaluated on four benchmarks (Synapse, ACDC, LA2018, and MSD Heart) under both 2D and 3D settings, LeViT-UNet++ achieves competitive accuracy with a compact parameter footprint and fast inference. On Synapse, for instance, it attains a DSC of 76.57% with only 8.025M parameters and 241.72 FPS, confirming a favorable accuracy-efficiency balance. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining wavelet-based multi-scale feature extraction with lightweight local-global feature fusion for efficient medical segmentation. The source code is available at https://github.com/apple1986/levit_unet_pp.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 24 pages, 5 figure

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: VIBRA: Backward-Compatible Cross-Modal Retrieval with Consensus Barycenters
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Backward-compatible retrieval enables a new encoder to query the gallery that an old model has already encoded, so that a cross-modal retrieval system can be upgraded without re-encoding billions of items. Existing compatible methods either fit the old query and stay near the accuracy of the old model, or run the old and the new encoder for every query. We propose VIBRA, which matches relevance on the old gallery, corrects the errors of a single model with the barycenter of several views, which is itself a query in the old space, and trains the new encoder to inherit this consensus, so that models absent at deployment still shape every query. We show that the barycenter gains margin over the average of its views exactly when their hardest irrelevant items differ, and we characterize the share of this gain that one encoder can reach. On five benchmarks with five upgrades among six CLIP, MetaCLIP and SigLIP2 backbones, VIBRA is the best compatible method in all 50 settings, improving Recall@1 by up to 5.6 points over the strongest baseline and by up to 18.0 points over the old model, while adding less than 1 ms to the latency of the new encoder.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: From Docket Minutes to Case Trajectories: Building Analysis-Ready Criminal Court Data
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Criminal court records are often fragmented, noisy, and siloed, making it challenging for both legal experts and community stakeholders to access and analyze court data to identify trends and provide public oversight. In this paper, we introduce a system for data ingestion, harmonization, and dashboard visualization designed for New Orleans criminal court proceedings data, aimed at both expert and lay audiences. Our system collects and harmonizes disparate data, generates case trajectories, and provides intuitive visualization techniques based on community feedback to analyze demographics, temporal trends, and specific case events. We demonstrate the system through an exploratory analysis of recent short-term trends and policy impacts within New Orleans, illustrating how it can support the investigation of anomalies, policy changes, and procedural irregularities. We also present feedback from a small formative study of community stakeholders who have helped co-design and use the system, suggesting that it may improve access to and interpretation of local court data.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: This paper has been accepted at IEEE Big Data 2026

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Access to large-scale clinical text collections is crucial for advancing medical information retrieval research, including clinical note search, patient cohort identification, and domain-adapted retrieval models. However, real clinical notes are rarely available due to privacy regulations, which particularly limits progress for low-resource languages such as European Portuguese. We present LusoClin, a publicly released dataset of synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, created to support privacy-preserving research on clinical text retrieval. LusoClin was generated by pre-processing real clinical data, fine-tuning the open-source Llama 3.2 (3B) instruction-tuned model using Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation, and applying prompt-based clinical note generation. To facilitate semantic indexing and clinical search, the notes are automatically annotated with clinical entities using a BERT-based model. We evaluate LusoClin in terms of utility, fidelity, diversity, and privacy using automatic metrics and human evaluation. Results indicate that the dataset captures clinically relevant language patterns and can support downstream IR applications such as clinical document retrieval and domain-specific model adaptation, although annotators can often distinguish synthetic from real notes and some medical inconsistencies persist.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: LEGIT: Live Eligibility Gating over Identifier Tries for Constrained Decoding of Heterogeneous Pages
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: A generative recommender names each candidate with a short token sequence, a Semantic ID, and recommends by generating those tokens. Some generative recommenders, including the Uber Eats search engine we are building, write a whole results page, stores with their menu items, in one decoding pass. Every Semantic ID on such a page must name a real store or item that is eligible for the search, such as a store that delivers to the user's location, and that is not already on the page. Each item must also belong to the store above it. A trie over the catalog keeps identifiers real, but eligibility and repetition change with every request and token, and the grammar-constrained decoder we tried could not enforce these changing rules exactly and quickly. We call this constraint LEGIT, for live eligibility gating over identifier tries. Numbering trie leaves depth first turns each rule into a range lookup over one store trie and one item trie, and every generated page passes an independent catalog check. On one NVIDIA B200 GPU with one or two requests per decode step, a direct implementation that walks the trie on the GPU makes each token about 5 times as slow as unconstrained decoding. Across 36 implementations, hardware counters and ablations are consistent with kernel launches and CPU-GPU waits as the source of this slowdown. Our fastest implementation walks the trie on the CPU while the GPU runs the model, needs no custom kernel, and cuts time per output token by 65.9 percent against the direct GPU implementation, to about 1.7 times the unconstrained cost. This implementation is also the fastest on a page layout that puts each item before its store.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Reliable visual document understanding requires a model to attribute each answer to the evidence regions that support it. Recent benchmarks and systems express this step through a coordinate interface: the model outputs the coordinates of bounding boxes that mark the evidence regions in the document. Under this interface, vision-language models often fail to identify the right regions even when the answer is correct, a failure known as Attribution Hallucination. We present a study that investigates whether this failure is partially limited by what the model can express through coordinates. On a verified bilingual CiteVQA subset, we compare the coordinate interface with a language interface in which the model outputs only text, quoting its evidence verbatim, and a multimodal retriever returns the location of each quote as a page region proposed by a layout parser (tables and figures are quoted through their captions or notes); the comparison is repeated over six open vision-language models. Compared with the coordinate interface, evidence recall rises from at most 8 points to between 26 and 47 and the hallucination rate roughly halves, with little change in answer quality. Building on this comparison, we use the same quote-and-retrieve pipeline as a training scaffold: because region-level evidence labels are expensive to collect for long documents, we introduce a GRPO recipe whose reward is a judge's reading of the gold answer and crops of the retrieved regions, training the model to quote better evidence without any region labels and raising an 8B backbone's strict attributed accuracy from 22.4 to 33.8. These findings indicate a practical path to improve attribution without a coordinate interface and without costly region-level supervision.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: CARE: Conversational Affective Response Retrieval for Internet Memes
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Conversational meme retrieval supports response selection in online communication, where relevance depends on both contextual meaning and affective expression. We study this task using two language-specific collections from Douban and Imgflip, containing 98,506 meme records across 5,583 discussion topics. Thread membership supplies weak relevance labels, while likes provide implicit ranking feedback. Automatically extracted sentiment, facial-expression indicators, and cross-modal consistency features support an exploratory analysis of engagement. We propose CARE, a Conversational Affective Response Retrieval framework that combines an emotion-enhanced CLIP retriever with a Jina-based reranker. The retriever incorporates free-form emotion descriptors through gated fusion and learns from multiple positive examples per query. The reranker combines query--image interactions with emotion representations and is trained using engagement-based ranking supervision. Under the reported topic-held-out protocol, CARE achieves Hit@10 of 24.03\% on Douban and 49.33\% on Imgflip, compared with 23.16\% and 41.07\%, respectively, for fine-tuned CLIP. These results support the utility of the complete two-stage system for recovering thread-associated memes. They do not independently establish perceived social resonance or isolate the contribution of affect from reranker training. The study provides a basis for further evaluation of affect-aware retrieval with human relevance judgments and controlled comparisons.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Prioritize, Don't Decide: What We Learned Auditing a Deployed Human-in-the-Loop CV Sorter
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: A single academic vacancy can draw hundreds of applications, and the first screening round consumes most of a committee's time. We describe a CV Priority Sorter deployed at a national platform for academic vacancies and integrated with its vacancy database. It proposes a reading order for a pile of CVs and leaves every decision to the committee, pairing a frozen multilingual transformer encoder with a per-session linear model that retrains after each label and is discarded when the session ends. It works: on a pool of 300 synthetic CVs, a committee reading in the tool's order reaches 95% of the relevant candidates after half the pile, where an arbitrary order needs almost all of it. This paper is about what we found when we audited that claim, rather than about the system itself. Three findings changed the product. The pool turned out to be sortable by document length alone, which makes precision-style metrics on it uninformative; regenerating it under a shared length budget removes that shortcut and leaves the reading-depth result standing. The four-level agreement score such systems report, ours included, is a binary probability cut at fixed thresholds, so it follows the classifier's confidence rather than its ranking and falls as labels accumulate. And uncertainty sampling, the obvious way to implement a "suggest the next CV" button, leaves model quality intact but raises the committee's total reading load above the no-label baseline, because the CVs it asks about are the ones that would otherwise be skipped. A fourth result shows where to look next: a hosted LLM embedding model lifts zero-label ordinal discrimination from 0.66 to 0.80 under length control, then stops mattering once the session model has two dozen labels; a local cross-encoder matches that cold-start gain without sending data out. We report the fixes each finding forced.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Under review at the EACL 2027 Industry Track

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: When the tail is earned by its companions: measuring label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: A rare label seldom occurs alone, and a classifier can recover it from the frequent labels it co-occurs with, its companions, without having learned the label itself. Existing diagnostics of this need a trained model: none says before training whether a corpus admits the failure, or what the standard aggregate hides. Macro-F1, like any measure built from per-label confusion counts, is unchanged by how a label's recall divides between occurrences with and without a companion. We introduce a within-label estimand of that division, a reading rule under which a fall in dependence counts only if companion-free recall rises, and a statistic of training labels that bounds, before training, how far reported recall can exceed companion-free recall. Across 23 corpora, 7 training objectives and five families of label-correlation mechanisms, companion-free recall falls short on all six corpora where the estimand is defined. Up to 18.4% of the tail true positives macro-F1 credits would vanish at the companion-free rate, within the training-label bound on every corpus. No long-tail objective reduces the dependence, but architecture moves it. Models whose tail score is computed from other labels' predictions are strongly dependent.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: 27 pages, 3 figures, 13 tables. Submitted to Information Sciences

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Music Similarity Learning in Sparse Latin Scenarios
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: In this work we propose a lightweight, interpretable approach that estimates item-item music similarity from publicly available metadata. Our hybrid regression model combines content-based filtering with the classic item-based collaborative filtering. We test generalization via a zero-shot evaluation on Latin American music, a genre for which co-occurrence data is scarce. Accurately predicting similarity for these unseen, sparse pairs shows that our approach is robust to the regional gap affecting many existing systems, without the audio signal processing or the computational budget that deep multimodal approaches would require.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Efficient sequential recommendation has emerged as a promising paradigm for providing real-time personalized service. To deploy models under resource-constrained environment, model compression becomes a necessity, yet existing methods typically apply uniform compression ratios, overlooking the heterogeneity in user intent complexity. This "one-size-fits-all" approach leads to a fundamental Capacity-Complexity Mismatch, where computational resources are either wasted on simple instances or insufficient for complex ones. To address this, we propose RACE (Ranking-uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation), a framework that dynamically adapts both model structures and input sequences with uncertainty-aware compression ratios. To ensure capacity-adaptive inference, RACE captures the model's intrinsic uncertainty of its predictions and transforms it into a proactive resource allocator. Specifically, we derive a list-wise ranking-uncertainty metric from the distributional stability of top-$K$ predictions, which serves as a measurable proxy for instance complexity. A lightweight predictor is then trained via self-supervision to anticipate this uncertainty from early-layer features. Guided by this signal, RACE performs instance-specific slimming in two dimensions: a hypernetwork-style channel sensitivity extractor identifies parameter redundancy, while importance-aware progressive sequence filtering mitigates data redundancy. Extensive experiments on four popular datasets demonstrate that RACE outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on accuracy, efficiency, and adaptability.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Better Rankers, Worse Retrievers: The Hidden Cost of RL Post-Training in Generative Recommendation
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Generative recommenders decode the semantic ID of a user's next item with a language model, and post-training them with reinforcement learning (RL) after supervised fine-tuning (SFT) has become standard practice. The gains are mostly reported on the first ten results, yet in deployment such models hand hundreds of candidates to a downstream ranker or reward model. We show that RL post-training has a hidden cost: it improves accuracy at the top of the list (hit@K for small K) but, on all five datasets we study, lowers the recall of the candidate list (hit@K for K in the hundreds). The model becomes a better ranker and a worse retriever. Controlled experiments trace the loss to the negative advantages that RL assigns to the candidates it samples, the rollout. The root cause is that only one next item is logged per user, so RL treats every other candidate as wrong. Yet these candidates are the model's most plausible alternatives, and often the next items of other users with similar histories. Penalising them pushes down exactly what similar users choose next, and these items drop out of those users' candidate lists. This diagnosis points directly to a remedy: out-of-rollout anchoring, a single additional loss term that preserves the SFT model's ordering of the items outside the rollout. It keeps the gain at the top and restores recall to the SFT level on all five datasets, and it is effective under other RL configurations as well. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of this recall loss: we measure it, identify its cause, and show that, once the cause is known, a simple remedy suffices.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: IntentGR: Enhancing Intent for End-to-End Personalized Generative Retrieval in Search
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Personalized generative retrieval in search should jointly satisfy the user's immediate search intent and long-term preference. Recent end-to-end approaches, primarily explored in recommendation, unify item tokenization and sequence generation within a single model, allowing semantic identifiers (SIDs) to be optimized toward the downstream generation objective. However, these methods often treat the query merely as an input feature, without explicitly leveraging it to guide either identifier learning or sequence generation. This leaves intent guidance weak in both the tokenization and the generation stage, causing generated semantic identifiers to drift toward high-frequency token patterns rather than the current search intent. In this work, we find that incorporating additional query-related evidence into the framework of end-to-end generative retrieval is important. Based on this finding, we propose IntentGR, an intent-enhanced end-to-end framework that strengthens query semantics at four complementary stages of the retrieval pipeline. Query-Aware Semantic Behavior Representation (QBR) introduces query-level behavioral evidence as a new input signal; Query-Semantic Alignment (QSA), Long-Tail Query Enrichment (LQE), and Query-conditioned Attention Modulation (QAM) then serve as integration mechanisms at the optimization, training-distribution, and decoding stages to fully exploit this evidence. Experiments on the public AOL4PS benchmark and AE, a large-scale industrial e-commerce dataset, show that IntentGR improves Recall@10 by 8.11% and 11.96% over the strongest baseline, with strong gains on long-tail queries. These results suggest that enriched query-related input evidence, together with effective integration mechanisms, is beneficial for building intent-aware end-to-end generative search systems.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: 11 pages, 3 figures; Accepted by WSDM 2027 Findings

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Learning Cross-Domain Media Similarity from Amazon Reviews
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Collaborative filtering is a basic foundation of many recommendation algorithms. It works by analyzing a user's history and then suggesting items similar to those in that history. This method typically relies on user data to compute item similarity, data that is widely available to commercial systems but is usually sparse or inaccessible for independent systems and research, especially across multiple media domains. In this work, we propose a method to generalize similarity information between items using supervised learning. As input to our model, we use semantic and temporal features extracted from Amazon product reviews, which are publicly available. As the training target, we use item (product) co-occurrence in the reviewing history of Amazon customers. We evaluate the quality of the predicted similarities across two media domains: books and movies. Experimental results demonstrate the robustness of our methodology, yielding positive outcomes in zero-shot cross-domain transfer tasks. Furthermore, feature attribution analysis reveals a structural shift in how feature groups are utilized across setups: intra-domain models rely heavily on linguistic semantics, whereas cross-domain environments pivot toward behavioral popularity cues. Incorporating even limited target-domain context during training bridges this domain sparsity gap, significantly enhancing framework generalization.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: NewsReX: An Open-Source Multi-Framework for Neural News Recommendation
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Reproducing and comparing results in neural news recommendation research remains difficult due to fragmented codebases, inconsistent preprocessing pipelines, and tight coupling between models and deep learning frameworks. We present NewsReX, an open-source framework that unifies multiple neural news recommendation models across two ML backends (PyTorch and JAX/Flax). Models are defined through a structured YAML specification that captures architecture, training recipe, and data contract, decoupling model definition from framework-specific implementation. A Hydra-based configuration system enables composable experiments with single-command framework switching. We provide cross-framework parity tests to verify numerical consistency across backends, allowing researchers to reproduce results from the original implementations and then transfer experiments to their preferred framework. We report comprehensive experiments on the MIND-small benchmark with multiple seeds per model and per framework, and demonstrate multilingual generalization by training on a proprietary Japanese news dataset from Nikkei News. We also publish pre-trained model weights on Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/newsrex) so that researchers can build on existing results without redundant retraining, reducing both computational cost and energy consumption. All source code, experiment configurations, and trained model weights are publicly available.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at CIKM 2026 (Resource Track), Rome, Italy. Code: https://github.com/igor17400/NewsReX

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Optimizing recommender models remains heavily reliant on manual iteration over architectures, objectives, and training strategies. While LLM-based agents can automate this trial-and-error process, relying on LLMs to both select modification directions and formulate concrete hypotheses can lead to unstable search under limited trial budgets. Inspired by the above challenge, we propose RecHarness, a Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for automated recommender model optimization. RecHarness decouples the optimization process into two steps: a bandit router selects the next modification direction according to historical validation feedback, while the LLM generates a concrete optimization hypothesis and executable code edit within the selected direction. To sustain long-horizon exploration, RecHarness uses a jump-basin mechanism to activate a structural-jump arm when local edits stagnate. Across multiple recommendation tasks, datasets, and model backbones, RecHarness achieves more consistent performance improvements and uses limited trial budgets more effectively than LLM-directed search. During a 7-day online A/B test on a large-scale short-video advertising platform, the selected candidate improves ADVV by 2.084%, Revenue by 0.534%, and Exposure by 0.559%. Code is available at: https://github.com/6lyc/RecHarness.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. Generative recommendation (GR) offers a promising paradigm by autoregressively generating discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) of items.
