First, motivated by the close relationship between image textures and frequency characteristics, we develop a Fractal Frequency-Aware Band Image Compression (FFAB-IC) network to capture directional frequency components in natural images. By integrating fractal band operations into nonlinear neural transformations, the network preserves essential image information while suppressing redundant details. Second, we incorporate diffusion knowledge into the encoder and introduce iterative diffusion refinement into the decoder, enabling the recovery of realistic textures under constrained bitrates. Third, we introduce frequency- and content-aware regularization to jointly exploit spatial structures and frequency characteristics during optimization. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that our method achieves a superior rate-distortion-realism trade-off, delivering higher realism at comparable distortion than existing approaches.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: HR-NVC++: Unified Ultra-High-Resolution Neural Video Coding with Confidence-Guided Spatial-Temporal Cues
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Ultra-high-resolution neural video coding (NVC) remains challenging because temporal correspondence becomes increasingly unreliable as spatial resolution increases. Although recent neural B-frame codecs have improved bi-directional temporal prediction, complex motion and fine-grained structures still lead to unreliable temporal references, while spatial information of the current frame remains underexploited. In this work, we propose HR-NVC++, a unified ultra-high-resolution NVC approach that supports both fidelity-oriented and perceptual-quality-oriented compression with a shared spatial-temporal context. The context integrates bi-directional temporal cues with complementary spatial information: confidence-guided fusion adaptively balances the forward and backward temporal cues according to their estimated correspondence reliability, while a spatial complement branch enriches regions that temporal references fail to explain. The resulting context serves as a common basis for two compression modes. Built upon this shared context, the fidelity mode retains entropy-based latent coding for pixel-accurate compression, whereas the perceptual mode removes additional latent coding and performs reconstruction directly from the context. This design demonstrates that a sufficiently informative spatial-temporal context already carries the dominant content required for perceptually favorable reconstruction, allowing different compression objectives to share the same contextual representation. Extensive experiments on UVG-4K and JVET Class A1/A2 show that HR-NVC++ achieves an average PSNR BD-rate saving of 13.01% over the H.266/VVC reference model VTM-13.2 under the random access configuration, while delivering substantially better perceptual quality and temporal consistency than existing neural video codecs.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Ultrasound Elastography: Excitation Methods and Low-Cost Alternative
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Ultrasound elastography (or elasticity imaging) is a method that characterizes the tissue mechanical properties with the purpose of aiding the diagnosis of certain pathologies. Many novel clinical applications use the assumption that these tissue properties are changed in the presence of pathological processes. Characterization of tissue mechanical properties is achieved by imaging the response of the tissue to an induced stress or excitation. A plethora of approaches have been used in the scientific community to induce excitation in tissue, which usually require additional tools or devices than are costly. Furthermore these are usually integrated in the imaging pipeline using additional software or hardware for control. An alternative that is simpler, faster to integrate (and low-cost) is proposed in this work, by using readily available smartphones as a source of mechanical excitation. The induced displacements are used to solve the elasticity inverse problem (IP) using a finite element method (FEM) approach. Preliminary elasticity reconstructions of a phantom that mimics tissue are similar to when using a dedicated actuator as means of inducing harmonic displacements, illustrating the feasibility of our low-cost ultrasound elasography approach.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Neuromorphic Camera for Multi-Target Pointing Acquisition and Tracking in Free Space Optical Communication
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Pointing, Acquisition, and Tracking (PAT) in Free-Space Optical Communication (FSOC) applications must achieve both low jitter and a large Field of View (FoV) to support beacon acquisition and multi-target tracking. While conventional frame-based sensors provide the necessary angular coverage, their performance is limited by latency, available frame-rate, and motion blur. This work explores and demonstrates the application of an event-based vision sensor for PAT tasks in FSOC. The system employs a neuromorphic sensor that asynchronously records brightness changes (events) with microsecond-level temporal resolution. The main contribution of this paper is a comparative analysis of event-based tracking algorithms for the simultaneous acquisition and tracking of multiple optical beacons that operate directly on this asynchronous stream. The performance of these strategies is validated on an experimental dataset representing realistic operational conditions for dynamic High-Altitude Platform (HAP) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. The analysis compares key metrics, such as tracking accuracy and processing latency, under various signal-to-background conditions.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 16 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables including 3 appendices

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Physics-Informed Generative Augmentation for Open-Set UAV Classification
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Open-set recognition of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) from passive 5G radar micro-Doppler signatures is challenging because unknown drone types cannot be anticipated at training time. We propose a physics-informed generative adversarial network (PI-GAN) that conditions spectrogram synthesis on rotor kinematics, forcing the classifier's feature space to encode physically meaningful structure. We compare PI-GAN augmentation against a vanilla conditional GAN (CGAN) and basic data augmentation across three held-out configurations with 1, 2, and 3 unknown classes. Vanilla CGAN augmentation collapses open-set clustering, reducing the adjusted Rand index (ARI) from 0.97 to 0.01, whereas PI-GAN preserves it at 0.97. In a controlled held-out sweep with two unknown classes, PI-GAN achieves an ARI of 0.92 compared to 0.07 for vanilla CGAN. The physics-informed features enable unsupervised separation of mechanically distinct unknown drones without retraining, demonstrating that physics-conditioned generation is the key enabler of open-set capability.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted by ICT Express

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Real Pairs Are Not Enough: Physically Anchored Supervision for Volumetric CT Super-Resolution
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Volumetric CT super-resolution (SR) models are commonly trained on synthetic or physically acquired pairs of low-resolution (LR) and high-resolution (HR) volumes. However, synthetic pairs miss real acquisition effects, whereas registered physical pairs retain inter-scan noise, artifact, and microstructure differences---causing direct voxelwise regression, and even naive synthetic-real mixing, to oversmooth fine porous structures. We introduce the Physically-anchored Implicit Network (PIN) with Real-Pair Dual-Anchor learning, which decouples physical-pair supervision into two complementary roles. The HR anchor teaches fine structure from registered HR through pair-conditioned spectral replay, while the LR anchor constrains the prediction from acquired LR via affine-calibrated low-pass projection. Together with exact synthetic supervision in one shared volumetric implicit model, PIN learns from both physical scans without forcing the acquired-LR reconstruction to match registered HR voxel by voxel. Inference requires only acquired LR. Across 30 external baseline configurations on real CT, PIN achieves the lowest full-volume LPIPS, reduces average symmetric surface distance by 42.3-49.5% and bone-volume-fraction error by 52.2-53.4% relative to the three strongest baselines for each metric, and lowers the erased reference-pore volume fraction from 37.3-72.9% to 10.4%. Code, pretrained models, and evaluation scripts will be publicly available.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 47 pages, 5 figures, including supplementary material

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Learning Motion-Appearance Coupling Priors for Solving Video Inverse Problems
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Reconstructing video from degraded measurements requires priors that capture both frame appearance and temporal dynamics. Many recent approaches combine pretrained image diffusion priors with motion guidance, sidestepping the costs of training large video models. Temporal consistency is often enforced via photometric losses or warping-based constraints, which implicitly assume that motion explains frame-to-frame or latent-to-latent changes up to small deviations, an assumption that fails under occlusions, lighting changes, and non-rigid deformation. In this paper, we propose to learn the coupling between motion and frame appearance as a generative prior. We learn the distribution of motion-induced appearance residuals with a conditional diffusion model and use it to regularize reconstruction in video inverse problems. Our motion-appearance prior acts as a plug-in regularizer for diffusion-based video reconstruction, preserving the benefits of image diffusion models while remaining compatible with existing appearance regularization techniques. Experiments on dynamic video inverse problems show that reconstruction with a learnt motion-appearance coupling prior outperforms photometric-consistency and noise-warping baselines, and that the approach also transfers to cardiac MRI reconstruction.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: NeurIPS 2026

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Supervision-Aware Evaluation of MedGemma for Reference-Assisted Radiotherapy Contour Ranking
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Radiotherapy contour ranking can support quality assurance, but vision-language model (VLM) gains may reflect supervision, score construction, available inputs, or representation access. We evaluated frozen MedGemma 1.5 in a single-institution study, a 12-patient held-out HaN-Seg test, five-fold cross-fitting on 30 non-test HaN-Seg patients, and transfer without refitting to 120 SegRap2023 patients. On held-out HaN-Seg, a supervised readout of the final prompt state exceeded a supervised readout of the model's yes/no output probabilities by +0.3047 pooled average precision (AP; 95% patient-bootstrap interval [+0.2822, +0.3269]); the advantage persisted against a parameter-count-matched nonlinear control. A readout of projected visual tokens exceeded the final-state readout in cross-fitting and transfer (+0.0706 AP averaged equally across patients on SegRap; 95% interval [+0.0607, +0.0804]), while a structured panel-feature readout remained competitive with visual tokens. The anatomy-conditioned readout did not demonstrate an advantage over the native-feature comparator. These results motivate visual-token and structured-feature controls in medical-imaging VLM evaluations; outcomes were computational or synthetic, not clinical acceptability.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Interpreting Selective-Review Coverage for Head-and-Neck Auto-Contours
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Selective-review systems aim to reduce human review by passing candidates predicted to be low risk. However, coverage (the fraction passed) can be misleading when measurements needed to interpret risk are unavailable. We separate structural evaluability (a nonempty mask with all required measurements available), computational-endpoint status, and pass-or-review decisions using archived Mayo records and controlled OpenKBP analyses. In 3,968 Mayo records, all 1,167 recorded empty predictions (predicted target-organ masks containing zero voxels despite nonempty reference masks) were endpoint-negative and passed both modules, accounting for approximately 76% of each pass set. In a held-out OpenKBP test, a logistic-regression router achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.833 and average precision of 0.449 but passed all 544 non-evaluable candidates, including 542 prespecified empty-mask controls and 2 erosions that became empty. A structural gate removed those passes without changing scores or the threshold, preserved all evaluable passes, and assigned 98.71% of endpoint-positive candidates to review. Under the original preprocessing and in patient-disjoint development evaluation, a router trained only on evaluable candidates and a router modeling an unavailable state likewise passed no non-evaluable candidates, with similar evaluable discrimination and at least 99.0% of endpoint-positive candidates assigned to review in pooled outer-fold predictions. These results show that coverage should be interpreted jointly with candidate eligibility, endpoint scope, missingness handling, and routing rules; they do not establish clinical validity, deployment safety, or natural-failure prevalence.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Structural Guidance for Unified Joint Demosaicing and Denoising
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Joint demosaicing and denoising is a fundamental step in camera image signal processing, yet remains challenging because different Bayer-like color filter arrays (CFAs) and sensor noise jointly corrupt both color sampling and image content. Existing unified restoration networks explicitly model CFA geometry but are still driven primarily by pixel-level supervision, making them prone to structural degradation around edges, repetitive textures, and moiré patterns where local evidence is unreliable. We attribute this limitation partly to the absence of explicit structural guidance beyond pixel-level reconstruction supervision. Motivated by this observation, we propose a structural-guided unified restoration framework that injects pretrained structural knowledge into CFA-aware image restoration. Our model receives a unified five-channel observation consisting of the raw mosaic, CFA masks, and a noise-level map. A SwinIR restoration branch reconstructs pixel details under CFA-conditioned modulation, while a parallel structural reasoning branch extracts complementary structural cues from a sparse pseudo-RGB observation. To bridge the substantial domain gap between sparse noisy sensor data and the natural-image pretraining domain of the structural encoder, we introduce a lightweight trainable adapter before residually fusing structural and restoration features. A shared decoder jointly predicts the restored RGB image and an auxiliary clean mosaic, providing supervision in both image and sensor domains. Extensive experiments across multiple CFA patterns and noise levels demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art unified and CFA-specific methods, indicating that adapted structural priors can enhance robust camera image restoration. The source codes and dataset are provided in the supplementary material.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 19 pages, including supplementary material

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Coarse-to-Fine 3D MRI Reconstruction via Resolution-Agnostic Neural Operators
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Deep-learning-based 3D MRI reconstruction is limited in practice by the GPU memory and compute cost of full-volume training; 3D acquisitions are thus most often reconstructed by 2D models applied slice-by-slice and then stacked, which ignores through-plane (stacking-axis) structure. We reconstruct in full 3D and ask whether a model can be trained at low resolution (fast and memory-feasible) yet deployed at higher resolution. This coarse-to-fine strategy needs reliable cross-resolution performance, but standard networks are resolution-specific and degrade substantially when evaluated outside the training setting. We therefore use resolution-agnostic neural operators (NOs) and propose KIR-NO (k-space-to-Image Reconstruction Neural Operator), a discretization-agnostic framework for accelerated 3D MRI reconstruction. KIR-NO is trained with full backpropagation on low-resolution volumes and applied zero-shot to higher-resolution volumes at inference. Its core building block is a 3D neural operator based on discrete-continuous convolutions: convolutional filters are parameterized in a continuous basis and sampled at arbitrary voxel resolutions while preserving the local inductive bias of convolution. KIR-NO integrates these learned operators with physics-based consistency: a k-space neural-operator head first refines the undersampled Fourier measurements, and image-space neural-operator cascades then refine the reconstruction through interleaved data-consistency updates. Across 3D knee and brain MRI benchmarks, KIR-NO improves over classical and CNN baselines: it improves over a state-of-the-art 3D CNN by 2.2 dB PSNR at half resolution under 4x acceleration on SKM-TEA, with gains persisting at 8x and 16x. These results show that resolution-agnostic operators make coarse-to-fine 3D MRI reconstruction - cheap low-resolution training with high-resolution deployment - practical across anatomies.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: NeurIPS 2026

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) are compared mainly by accuracy averaged across findings, a summary that can hide complete failure on a single diagnosis. We audit five open medical VLMs (MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MedVLM-R1) on 6,048 ChestX-ray14 questions balanced by sex, age, finding, and label. On the 432 pneumothorax-positive X-rays, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detect zero cases while MedGemma and Lingshu detect 38% and 67% of the same images. The two failing models answer "no" to all 864 pneumothorax cases (balanced accuracy 0.500, chance), yet produce fluent, anatomically specific explanations that name the signs of a collapsed lung and then deny them, with no hedge or abstention. This failure is not an artifact of prompting, image resolution, label ambiguity, or model scale. It persists across four prompt formats, at native resolution, and on single-label cases. A within-model control shows the same forced prompt gives HuatuoGPT 79% recall on nodule but only 6% on pneumothorax. It survives a tenfold scale increase (Qwen2.5-VL-72B detects 4%) and replicates on SIIM-ACR, an independent dataset with radiologist-drawn masks, where the failing models detect 0 of 432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0 of the 144 largest lesions. Reading the models' logits and internal states shows this is not blindness. The two failing models are highly confident yet no better than chance and a linear probe recovers pneumothorax from their hidden representations even where recall is zero, so the finding is represented internally but suppressed at the output. Aggregate accuracy therefore cannot establish that a medical VLM can see a given finding, because a model that misses one can still describe it convincingly. Reporting per-finding recall and specificity on balanced cases is needed to tell the difference.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Medical Reasoning with Vision Language Foundation Models (Med-Reasoner). 16 pages including NeurIPS checklist, 1 figure, 5 tables

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: One Block Is Enough: LoopMR for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Deep-learning unrolled networks are the leading approach to accelerated MRI reconstruction. State-of-the-art models such as PromptMR+ learn a distinct block for every cascade, so their size grows with the number of cascades. Sharing one block across iterations avoids adding parameters, but earlier shared-weight models typically used a tiny block and produced worse images than models with distinct weights. Therefore, it remained unclear whether weight sharing itself or the choice of block was the problem. Recent advances in looped transformers, which reuse the same block across layers, show that they can match or outperform their distinct-weight counterparts on several tasks. Motivated by this, we propose LoopMR, which reuses a single Restormer block at every iteration as its core. Besides the current image estimate, the block receives data-consistency inputs and latent images. On four datasets covering the brain (CC359), knee (fastMRI), heart (CMRxRecon2023) and carotid (in-house), LoopMR significantly outperforms E2E-VarNet, PromptMR and PromptMR+ in PSNR and SSIM at every acceleration factor (p < 0.01), with about 1/9 of PromptMR+'s parameters (10.3M versus 92.9M). It also keeps its lead at unseen acceleration factors and on an unseen dataset. With our transformer block, the shared model matches or outperforms its distinct-weight counterpart at 6, 12 and 24 iterations. At a fixed number of iterations, shared transformer blocks match or outperform their distinct-weight versions, while shared CNN blocks perform worse. These results suggest that looping one well-chosen block can outperform stacking distinct cascades in MRI reconstruction, with a fraction of the parameters.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Code: https://github.com/hym97/LoopMR

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: AITHER: Authority-Informed Evidence Routing for Mixed-Authority Vision-Language Reasoning
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Reliable vision-language reasoning requires a control decision that conventional grounding methods leave implicit: which input is entitled to determine the answer? Auxiliary text may be a defeasible claim about an image, a binding task instruction, or compatible context. Correcting every image-text conflict toward the image therefore repairs false claims but overwrites valid task rules. We formalize this setting as mixed-authority vision-language reasoning and introduce AITHER, an Authority-Informed Text-Image Hierarchy for Evidence Routing. Its final policy, the Semantic-Frame Router, is a training-free black-box control layer that (i) compiles explicit task directives, (ii) recovers standardized spatial frames from metadata-scrubbed pixels, (iii) resolves the semantic polarity of remaining notes, and (iv) routes among frozen observable candidates with fail-closed semantics. This ordered decomposition converts authority arbitration from an unconstrained prompt preference into a reproducible inference program. Across 1,620 MATRIX predictions, AITHER reaches 95.1% accuracy, exceeding the strongest task-and-frame baseline by 9.1 points with a 95% record-cluster interval of 6.8-11.5 points and no harmed records. It further reaches 100.0% on 1,800 controlled FRAME predictions and 93.3% on GQA-MATRIX. The results show that explicit authority routing can simultaneously improve false-claim correction, preserve task-defined answers, and eliminate clean-context overcorrection.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: LUMIR: Decoupled Multimodal Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Data for Next-POI Recommendation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: As multimodal tourism-related information collected from heterogeneous data sources has become increasingly available, learning effective representations has attracted attention for improving recommendation performance. Existing approaches often tightly couple multimodal fusion with the architecture and optimization objective of a specific downstream model, which limits the generality and reusability of the learned representations. To address these limitations, we propose LUMIR, a decoupled multimodal representation learning framework based on contrastive learning. Multimodal information collected from heterogeneous data sources is first semantically unified into a shared textual representation space using large language models (LLMs). An interaction-aware fusion mechanism is then designed to model cross-modal interactions, while sequential signals are incorporated as a structural constraint to guide representation learning. To evaluate the learned representations, experiments are conducted on a multimodal point-of-interest (POI) dataset under the next-POI recommendation setting across multiple sequential recommendation backbones. The results show that LUMIR consistently outperforms existing multimodal fusion baselines in both accuracy-oriented and beyond-accuracy metrics, demonstrating that decoupling representation learning from downstream optimization provides an effective paradigm for learning reusable multimodal representations. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/wzehui/LUMIR.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 16 pages. Accepted at the DaQuaMRec Workshop, co-located with ACM RecSys 2026

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Data Quality Challenges in Multimodal Tourism Recommender Systems
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Modern recommender systems increasingly consider diverse data modalities to enhance model performance. However, the quality of the underlying multimodal data (e.g. data from social media platforms) has received limited attention so far. Focusing on tourism recommendation, we examine real-world challenges encountered when using datasets from Yelp and Instagram. Issues include noise from fake reviews, hallucinated content from LLMs, modality contradictions, and demographic bias. We outline future directions such as quality-aware fusion, structured and controlled LLM-based content generation to reduce hallucinations, and user group differentiation to improve the robustness and reliability of multimodal recommendation systems.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 4 pages. Presented at the DaQuaMRec Workshop, co-located with ACM RecSys 2025

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Joint Activation and Weight Quantization for Learned Image Compression
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Learned image compression (LIC) models achieve competitive rate-distortion performance with increasingly large networks, making network quantization important for efficient deployment. Directly quantizing LIC models remains difficult in post-training quantization (PTQ) because compression performance is highly sensitive to quantization noise. Existing methods typically focus on optimizing either the weights or the activations, resulting in substantial rate-distortion degradation. To address this limitation, we introduce a two-stage pipeline that uses SmoothQuant to balance activation and weight ranges, followed by GPTQ to adapt the transformed weights. The proposed joint search framework optimizes the balancing transformation and adapted weights under the rate-distortion objective, accounting for the coupling between the two stages. Experiments across multiple LIC architectures and activation quantization configurations show that the joint search strategy consistently reduces rate-distortion degradation after quantization.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted at IEEE VCIP 2026. 5 pages, 3 figures

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Unified Synthesis of Compositional Speech and Sound from Free-Form Text Prompts
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Generating unified audio that naturally integrates speech and sounds from free-form text prompts remains challenging. For example, the prompt ``A fast drum roll ends with a cymbal crash, after which a man shouts: `Come on!'.'' describes several events that should appear in order and form a coherent recording rather than independent tracks that lack coherent temporal and semantic interactions. Current methods broadly follow two paradigms: pipeline methods couple separate text-to-sound and text-to-speech models, while unified models rely on a single generator that still requires structured, multi-field prompt inputs. Both paradigms require upstream prompt decomposition or rewriting, limiting free-form flexibility and risking cascading errors. To enable direct generation from free-form prompts within a single model, we introduce PlanAudio, an end-to-end framework that maps unconstrained free-form text to unified audio without intermediate prompt preprocessing. To address the challenges of direct free-form generation, PlanAudio integrates latent planning into a single autoregressive framework, predicting continuous audio layout before acoustic token synthesis. We construct a large-scale training corpus and introduce Free-Form Unified Audio Generation Benchmark (FUAG) for evaluation, both spanning speech, sound, and joint speech-and-sound generation. Experiments show that a single PlanAudio outperforms existing pipeline and unified baselines on speech-and-sound generation, while remaining competitive with specialist models on speech and sound generation. Further analysis validates the effectiveness of audio layout planning over textual planning, acoustic planning, and direct generation. Sample Available: https://planaudio.github.io/PlanAudio2026/.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026. This version renames concepts, reorganizes sections, and fixes Method notation; adds ablation experiments and core-mechanism analysis; updates Table 1 with larger training data (improved speech performance in speech-and-sound mixed scenarios). The main conclusions remain unchanged

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: DASWeave: Weaving Evidence across Speaking Conditions for Multimodal Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Screening
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Multimodal screening for depression, anxiety, and stress in children and adolescents uses verbal and nonverbal behaviour. Most existing multimodal methods learn from a single recording or interview. Yet a participant's behaviour changes with the speaking condition, and these changes hold evidence that is invisible in a single recording. We propose DASWeave to bring this evidence into a neural network that encodes each response and then combines all responses of a participant. We train supervised trees to find which behavioural statistics matter for screening, both within each response and in how they change across conditions. We feed the tree outputs into the network both before and after this combination. We fine-tune a large language model to relate what a participant says to how they say it across conditions, and feed its representation into the network after the combination. The language model reads behaviour as text descriptions. We therefore derive additional training targets for the network from a multimodal large language model that takes in the audio-visual features directly. On the official hidden test set of the ACM Multimedia 2026 AdoDAS Grand Challenge (Track 1), DASWeave ranks second among 95 eligible teams. Its mean F1 is 27.1% higher than that of the official audio-visual baseline. It also has the highest mean AUROC among the top five teams. Ablation studies on the validation set show that the supervised trees and the fine-tuned language model contribute most to mean F1.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Smiling Regulates Emotion During Traumatic Recollection
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: We study when, where, and why 978 Holocaust survivors smile in video testimonies. We create an automatic smile detection model from facial features with an F1 of 85% and annotate detected smiles under two established taxonomies of smiling. We produce narrative features on 1,083,417 transcript sentences as well as emotional valence from three different modalities: audio, eye gaze, and text transcript. Smiling rates are associated with specific semantic topics, narrative structures, and temporal syntaxes across the corpus. Smiles often occur during periods of intense negative affect and we find negative-affect smiles are associated with more positive subsequent valence trajectories across all three modalities. Smiling reduces eye dynamics and blink rates, with both of these effects modulated by narrative valence. Taken together, we conclude that smiling plays a critical role in regulating emotion and social interaction during traumatic recollection.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Received Best Paper Runner-Up Award at ICMI 2026

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Calibrated selective prediction using deep ensembles for thyroid nodule ultrasound classification under dataset shift
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Background: Deep learning can classify thyroid nodules on ultrasound, but discrimination alone does not establish clinical reliability. We developed a calibrated deep-ensemble framework with uncertainty-aware selective prediction and conservative image-based triage. Methods: Nested five-fold cross-validation with three-fold inner architecture selection chose ConvNeXt-Tiny with a squeeze-and-excitation block, used to build a deterministic five-member ensemble. Training, early-stopping, calibration, and threshold subsets were separated within each fold; outer-test data remained isolated. Mutual information (MI), predictive variance, and maximum-softmax-probability (MSP) uncertainty were compared by risk-coverage and triage analyses, and predictive values across assumed malignancy prevalences of 5%-70%. The frozen TN5000 ensemble was applied to TN3K without recalibration. Results: On TN5000, pooled out-of-fold AUC-ROC was 0.9377, average precision 0.9708, expected calibration error 0.0138, and Brier score 0.0827. Under the primary MI-guided policy, 8.86% of images received a No-FNA suggestion, 60.00% an FNA recommendation, and 31.14% radiologist review; of 3574 malignant images, 14 (0.39%) received No-FNA and 708 (19.81%) review. Predictive variance and MSP ranked errors better than MI (AURC, AUGRC); no measure optimized all triage outcomes. Across prevalences of 5%-70%, NPV ranged 99.95%-97.93% and PPV 29.28%-94.75%. On TN3K, AUC-ROC was 0.7870, average precision 0.7254, expected calibration error 0.1899, and radiologist-review rate 83.7%. Conclusion: The ensemble showed strong internal discrimination and calibration, but performance deteriorated substantially on TN3K, indicating limited transportability under dataset shift. Multicentre validation, site-specific recalibration, threshold validation, and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical use.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Revised and corrected version, matching the published paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ibmed.2026.100517

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: ABRR: Transforming Temporal Sentence Grounding with Wasserstein-Adaptive Refinement and Precision Ranking
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Temporal Sentence Grounding (TSG) aims to localize temporal segments in untrimmed videos that correspond to natural language queries, a critical task for video understanding with applications in video retrieval, summarization, and human-computer interaction. Despite significant progress driven by transformer-based models, existing TSG methods suffer from two key limitations: quantization errors due to temporal downsampling, which misalign segment boundaries, and suboptimal ranking of predictions based on semantic matching rather than localization precision. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Boundary Refinement and Ranking (ABRR) framework, a novel, model-agnostic post-processing approach that enhances the performance of any TSG model without retraining. ABRR integrates three innovative components: (1) Temporal Distribution Smoothing, which mitigates noise in predicted score distributions using Gaussian kernel convolution; (2) Boundary Refinement via Optimal Transport, which leverages the 2-Wasserstein distance and Sinkhorn iterations to align coarse segment boundaries with true temporal moments, grounded in Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport theory; and (3) Quality-Driven Re-Ranking, which reorders predictions using a composite score balancing localization precision and semantic relevance. By correcting quantization errors and prioritizing accurately localized segments, ABRR achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art TSG models. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions, and QVHighlights, demonstrate consistent gains at stringent IoU thresholds (e.g., IoU=0.7), alongside enhanced ranking performance. The framework's computational efficiency and compatibility with existing models make it a versatile and impactful solution for real-world TSG applications.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Multimedia

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Multimodal Judges Flag, Humans Decide: A Review-and-Edit Framework for AI-Generated Product Video Ads
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Generative pipelines can now turn every product page of an e-commerce catalog into a short video ad, but deciding whether such an ad is usable is not one good-or-bad call. We describe how we operationalized the review and editing of these ads so that both can keep pace with generation: reviewers go through each ad scene by scene and answer six questions, on the product, scene quality, pronunciation, script, sound and captions; judges built from vision-language, speech and language models file each finding under the matching question, and reviewers accept or reject each finding and add what the judges missed. Each confirmed issue then opens an edit tool matched to it. The questions and the routing from a finding to its fix do not depend on the models that generate the ad. Across 120 ads from our pipeline, reviewed with judge findings on screen, reviewers marked the product wrong on 60% of scenes, and script, caption or sound problems on under 10% each. On 60 of these ads, they marked the product wrong on 58% of scenes, far more than the 26% marked by two reviewers who later saw the ads with the judges hidden; one reviewer who saw the ads both ways marked 57% with judge findings and 19% without. On 120 blind-labeled scenes, a product judge that watches the clip with the catalog photos reached AUC 0.84, while video-quality and photo-similarity scores were close to chance. We tune the judges for recall: the product judge catches nearly all defects but also flags many clean scenes, so reviewers decide; together, the judges widen what reviewers mark and reviewers add what the judges miss. Without judge findings, one reviewer's marking faded over a session. We release a review-portal template and our review data (120 ads and 562 scenes with judge findings and human marks, plus 120 blind-labeled scenes with baseline scores) at https://github.com/anoubhav/ad-review-and-edit.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted at the WVAQ workshop at WACV 2027

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot generalization but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Existing adversarial fine-tuning methods often use pre-trained model guidance to preserve image--text alignment while improving robustness. Our analysis of visual representation drift reveals complementary limitations of two representative forms of guidance. Matching visual features constrains all directions equally, providing broad coverage without semantic emphasis. Matching prediction distributions prioritizes semantically relevant directions, but remains limited by the candidate texts and prediction probabilities. These limitations can hinder preservation of pre-trained image--text relationships and degrade zero-shot performance. We therefore propose Textual Response-Aware Guidance (TRAG), which constrains visual representation drift using the pre-trained text encoder's responses to local variations in input embeddings. TRAG constructs anchor-level constraints from the response directions and magnitudes around semantic anchors, then aggregates them using pre-trained image--anchor relevance, yielding an image-adaptive constraint. Extensive experiments across architectures and tasks demonstrate state-of-the-art clean and robust performance. Further analysis shows that TRAG helps preserve pre-trained image--text relationships.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Memory-Efficient Active Perception for Embodied Question Answering in Dynamic Human-Populated Scenes
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Embodied Question Answering (EQA) couples active visual perception, vision-language reasoning, and sequential decision making, and has traditionally been evaluated in temporally stable environments where visual evidence can be accumulated reliably. In realistic multimedia settings such as dynamic human-populated scenes, however, moving people and transient occlusions introduce human-induced perceptual variations: task-relevant multimodal cues become transient, viewpoint-dependent, and incompletely captured in individual views. Conventional store-then-retrieve strategies generate redundant visual evidence and incur high inference cost, making them ill-suited to such variations. This exposes two core problems for embodied agents: resolving viewpoint-dependent ambiguity, and maintaining compact evidence for efficient inference. To address these challenges, we present DIVRR (Dynamic-Informed View Refinement with Relevance-guided Rotation and adaptive memory selection), a training-free active evidence-acquisition framework for EQA. DIVRR combines question-conditioned room guidance with relevance-triggered view augmentation to guide exploration and additional observation. Selective memory admission uses the same relevance signal as view augmentation to retain high-scoring evidence, reducing stored entries while keeping the retrieved visual context compact. To evaluate EQA under human-induced perceptual variations, we introduce DynHuman-EQA, a dynamic human-populated EQA dataset constructed in Habitat, comprising dynamic and static subsets under shared scene layouts. Experiments on DynHuman-EQA and HM-EQA show that DIVRR outperforms existing baselines in both accuracy and memory efficiency. The gains are most pronounced in dynamic human-populated scenes.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Artifact Filtering versus Artifact-Compensated Training in JPEG to JPEG AI Recompression
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: In this paper, we consider the problem of recompression of images from JPEG to JPEG AI format. We show that direct recompression from JPEG to JPEG~AI trained on uncompressed images is accompanied by the preservation of the JPEG image artifacts in the resulting JPEG~AI image. In order to avoid it, we evaluate an approach where an artifacts removal neural network is first applied to the input JPEG image as an external pre-filter. However, in this case, the processing time is increased by 29 times. Therefore, we propose an artifact-compensated training for JPEG AI and show that it is able to combine pre-filtering against target distortions with efficient compression without increase in the processing time.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Preprint. Submitted to IEEE Multimedia on 21 February 2026. This is the author's draft version; it has not undergone peer review. 15 pages, 8 figures

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: We present BARS (Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis), a non-autoregressive rapping voice generation model based on Flow Matching, conditioned on a beat track (instrumental backing), lyrics, and a short reference voice for zero-shot timbre control. Unlike prior autoregressive rap synthesis, where rap pace and output duration are strictly determined by the beat, BARS enables independent control over the rap tempo, allowing flexible-length generation without explicit duration prediction or phoneme-level alignment. We encode lyrics using a pretrained ByT5 encoder with a lightweight Transformer adapter trained jointly with the model, without relying on speech-pretrained text encoders, enabling natural handling of non-standard orthography (e.g., slang, abbreviations) and numerals common in rap lyrics. To address alignment instabilities, such as token skipping or repetition, under strong beat conditioning, we propose Asymmetric Scaled RoPE for cross-attention, which introduces a positional structure to facilitate sequential lyric-audio alignment learning. Furthermore, the model supports partial re-generation via span masking, enabling lyric-level editing while preserving the surrounding vocal style. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high lyric fidelity, natural rap flow that is rhythmically coherent with the beat, and robust tempo control across a wide range of rapping styles and speeds.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Published in ISMIR 2026 (Best Paper Award nominee). Demo: https://bars-ismir2026.github.io/bars/

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: YTShorts-92K: An Interpretable Multimodal Dataset of YouTube Shorts
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Short-form video has become one of the dominant formats of online content, yet large-scale datasets enabling the analysis of what makes these videos successful remain limited. Existing resources often focus on post-publication popularity signals or rely on non-interpretable representations such as high-dimensional embeddings. Here, we introduce YTShorts-92K, a dataset of 92,654 YouTube Shorts collected from 345 creators and spanning 12 manually defined content categories. Each video is enriched with an interpretable multimodal feature set covering metadata, textual information, visual characteristics from frames and thumbnails, and cross-modal consistency measures. We describe the collection methodology, data cleaning process, and feature extraction pipeline, followed by descriptive analyses of the diversity of creators, topics, and extracted features. This dataset offers a reusable resource for studying short-form video content, online attention, and multimodal content analysis.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: When Coding Agents Get Arms: Safety Risks Across the Digital-Physical Boundary
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Advances in spatial understanding have enabled frontier models to power coding agents that control a real robot arm zero-shot and end-to-end, without task-specific demonstrations or retraining. This brings two new safety challenges. First, the extensive knowledge of frontier models lets these agents perform tasks that earlier VLA and WAM paradigms could not, opening the door to new forms of capability misuse. Second, coding agents can access digital resources such as web pages and emails. Threats in these resources, such as indirect prompt injection, can carry over into the physical world when the agent controls a robot. We therefore introduce ArmedAgent, the first systematic benchmark to evaluate both risks for coding agents performing zero-shot robot control. It covers robustness, malicious use, and indirect injection across 36 tasks in 5 scenarios, evaluated in simulation and validated on a physical robot arm. A distinctive portion of the tasks target harmful behaviors that earlier VLA paradigms could not perform. Testing several frontier models, including GPT-6-Astra, under widely used agent frameworks, we find substantial safety risks in current systems.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Technical report, work in progress

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Existing multimodal attribution methods typically rely on paired modalities as proxy supervision, implicitly assuming that image-text pairs are semantically aligned. Information bottleneck (IB)-based attribution methods follow this general paradigm and instantiate it through a global sufficiency-compression objective. In realistic multimodal datasets, however, this assumption is frequently violated due to partial semantic misalignment and unreliable cross-modal correspondences. Through theoretical analysis, we show that, under such misalignment, information-bottleneck-based attribution objectives exhibit a structural limitation: by assuming equal reliability across all proxy supervision signals, they induce posterior over-contraction and forced explanations. To address this issue, we propose TIB, a sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck framework that adaptively modulates attribution strength according to cross-modal reliability, without assuming semantic alignment. Extensive experiments on controlled benchmarks and large-scale datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed approach, while also validating the identified failure mode.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accpeted to NeurIPS2026

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: PhysElite: How Far Are LLMs from Solving Olympiad-Level Physics Problems?
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Understanding how (multimodal) large language models perform on physics problems requires benchmarks that reflect the difficulty and breadth of expert-level physical reasoning. Existing physics benchmarks remain limited in the following two important ways: (1) short of high-difficulty datasets, and (2) lack of comprehensive coverage of visual forms, knowledge points, and step-by-step solution processes. As a result, model performance on current datasets may not be fully representative of their ability to solve complex physics problems. To address these issues, we present PhysElite, a large-scale bilingual multimodal benchmark for Olympiad-level physics reasoning. PhysElite contains 11,586 Olympiad-tier problems. For each problem, we provide corresponding visual diagrams, step-by-step bilingual Chinese-English solution derivations, and the final answer. We benchmark 18 open-source and closed-source MLLMs, and find that even the strongest model reaches only 33.7% answer accuracy. We additionally conduct step-level process evaluation to diagnose where models fail in the reasoning chain. Our datasets are released at https://github.com/PremiLab-Math/PhysElite.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2026

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: JND-Guided Light-Weight Neural Pre-Filter for Perceptual Image Coding
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Just Noticeable Distortion (JND)-guided pre-filter is a promising technique for improving the perceptual compression efficiency of image coding. However, existing methods are often computationally expensive, and the field lacks standardized benchmarks for fair comparison. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a twofold contribution. First, we develop and open-source FJNDF-Pytorch, a unified benchmark for frequency-domain JND-Guided pre-filters. Second, leveraging this platform, we propose a complete learning framework for a novel, lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art compression efficiency, consistently outperforming competitors across multiple datasets and encoders. In terms of computational cost, our model is exceptionally lightweight, requiring only 7.15 GFLOPs to process a 1080p image, which is merely 14.1% of the cost of recent lightweight network. Our work presents a robust, state-of-the-art solution that excels in both performance and efficiency, supported by a reproducible research platform. The open-source implementation is available at https://github.com/viplab-fudan/FJNDF-Pytorch.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, Submitted to ISCAS2027

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Do Joint Audio-Video Generation Models Understand Physics?
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Joint audio-video generation models are rapidly approaching professional production quality, raising a central question: do they understand audio-visual physics, or merely generate plausible sounds and frames that violate real-world consistency? We introduce AV-Phys Bench, a benchmark for evaluating physical commonsense in joint audio-video generation. AV-Phys Bench tests models across three scene categories: Steady State, Event Transition, and Environment Transition. It covers physics-grounded subcategories drawn from real-world scenes, plus Anti-AV-Physics prompts that deliberately request physically inconsistent audio-video behavior. Each generation is evaluated along five dimensions: visual semantic adherence, audio semantic adherence, visual physical commonsense, audio physical commonsense, and cross-modal physical commonsense. Across three proprietary and four open-source models, we find that Seedance 2.0 performs best overall, but all models remain far from robust physical understanding. Performance drops sharply on event-driven and environment-driven transitions, and even strong proprietary systems collapse on Anti-AV-Physics prompts. We further introduce AV-Phys Agent, a ReAct-style evaluator that combines a multimodal language model with deterministic acoustic measurement tools, producing rankings that closely align with human ratings. Our results identify cross-modal physical consistency and transition-driven scene dynamics as key open challenges for joint audio-video generation.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ZijunCui/AV-Phys-Bench Code: https://github.com/ZijunCui02/AV-Phys Homepage: https://zijuncui.com/AV-Phys/ Full abstract appears in the PDF

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Data Diversity, Not Frequency Invariance: A Controlled and Self-Audited Study of Compression-Robust Deepfake Detection
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Frequency features and compression-invariant representation learning are widely assumed to be key to deepfake detection that survives video compression. We test this with CAFRL - block-DCT and FFT-phase streams, compression-level-conditioned band attention, and adversarial (gradient-reversal) compression invariance - and report a controlled negative. Under a pre-registered protocol with capacity- and augmentation-matched controls, a plain EfficientNet-B0 on multi-quality data beat CAFRL as specified at every compression level on the FaceForensics++ test split, by 3.66 AUC points at CRF 40 (paired, single seed). A self-audit of our own negative found four defects biased against the frequency hypothesis, and pre-specified re-tests repairing all four showed the deficit to be a recipe artifact, not an architecture failure: the baseline recipe recovered 3.96 points over the matching shipped-recipe variant. The frequency path made no detectable difference: discriminative alone (standalone validation AUC 0.91-0.98 late in training) but of no marginal value under this fusion, at two feature widths of one 4.0 M trunk, every seed-pooled interval for the intra-dataset compression contrasts including zero; on the single held-out manipulation tested, the fair variants sat below the plain backbone. The adversarial branch, as specified, added nothing and degraded its own conditioning estimator; at the fair recipe it is untested. Robustness under single-pass H.264 re-encoding came instead from data diversity: real constant-rate-factor variants beat synthetic JPEG augmentation by 7.3 points (single runs, non-overlapping intervals). The evidence is FaceForensics++-family, GAN-era and single-codec. Match controls on training recipe as well as capacity, and buy compression robustness with codec diversity before architecture.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 38 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IEEE Access. Code, per-video predictions and a claims-to-artifacts map: https://github.com/Capta1n-n9m0/cafrl-negative (v1.0.0); archival deposit: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22032529

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: MuSP-Bench: Advanced Multimodal Benchmarking of Music Understanding across Score and Performance
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Musicians commonly communicate musical intent through scores and performances. To investigate whether models can reason across both modalities, we introduce MuSP-Bench, a human-authored benchmark of 490 questions assessing understanding across Musical Scores and Performances, both individually and in combination. The benchmark spans interpretive and long-horizon reasoning across classical piano and orchestral works, represented through ABC notation, score images, MIDI, and audio. Our evaluation of frontier multimodal large language models reveals substantial difficulties in understanding musical scores and even greater challenges in reasoning about audio.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted to ISMIR 2026 Late-Breaking Demo. Benchmark site: https://musp.vaclis.net/

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: The RenAIssance: Caption-Guided Diffusion Models for Historical-Art Visual Media
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Generative AI can expand cultural collections into prompt-responsive visual media, but historical artworks rarely provide the paired descriptions needed to adapt modern image generators. We present The RenAIssance, a scalable pipeline that turns a collection of historical European artworks into a reusable text-to-image media resource. The pipeline generates scene-level captions with BLIP and uses the resulting approximately 15,000 image--text pairs from DEArt to train a compact LoRA adapter for Stable Diffusion v1.5. The adapter shifts generated images toward the historical-art distribution while retaining the base model's ability to render novel concepts. On historical and contemporary prompts of different lengths, it improves FID to the DEArt reference distribution in every setting with only a modest decrease in CLIP text--image similarity. Qualitative results show that the same adapter can render both period-appropriate subjects and contemporary concepts in a coherent historical visual language. By decoupling a reusable style representation from the base generator, the approach offers a practical building block for controllable historical-art media creation, interactive authoring, and rich-media experiences.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted at ACMMM26 RichMediaGAI. This work is co-funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under MSCA with grant agreement No 101081674

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Squeezing Capacity from Multimodal Large Language Models for Subject-driven Generation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Subject-driven image generation aims to synthesize new images that preserve the identity of the given subject while following textual instructions. Existing approaches often encode text and reference images separately. This limits cross-modal reasoning abilities and causes copy-paste artifacts. Recent frameworks that connect multimodal models and diffusion models improve instruction following, but largely overlook identity preservation. To address these limitations, we condition diffusion models on Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) that jointly encode text and reference images, and augment it with VAE-based identity conditioning. A novel Dual Layer Aggregation (DLA) module is designed to aggregate multi-level MLLM features for optimal conditioning, and a multi-stage denoising strategy is applied to progressively balance the semantic information from MLLM and fine-detail identity from VAE during inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach harmonizes multimodal understanding with identity preservation, mitigates copy-paste issues, and achieves superior performance regarding human preference on subject-driven image generation. Our project website is available at https://zsh2000.github.io/squeeze-mllm-subject-gen/.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: NeurIPS 2026, 42 pages, 18 figures, Project Page: https://zsh2000.github.io/squeeze-mllm-subject-gen/

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: To Think or Not to Think: Pre-Decisional Reasoning Budgets for Referring Audio-Visual Segmentation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Multimodal reasoning systems increasingly assume that longer chain-of-thought (CoT) uniformly improves downstream grounding. We show that this assumption fails in referring audio-visual segmentation (Ref-AVS): simple queries can be harmed by excessive reasoning, creating an "overthinking trap" associated with phrase and localization drift, while genuinely ambiguous queries still benefit from multi-step reasoning. To systematically study this, we construct counterfactual reasoning-budget labels under a five-fold out-of-fold evaluation protocol. Our results recast adaptive Ref-AVS reasoning as a pre-decisional representation problem: before the first generated token, the generation-onset state contains linearly decodable information predictive of whether additional reasoning will improve segmentation. A linear probe predicts binary reasoning need with 70.1% accuracy, substantially outperforming text-only features and uncertainty-based proxy signals. As a router, the onset-state controller improves over downstream confidence routing and closely matches Short-then-Decide while using far fewer tokens. Proxy comparisons show that the onset representation contains predictive information not fully recovered by the evaluated hand-crafted features. Reusing this onset state for lightweight, single forward-pass routing reduces autoregressive token consumption by 60% while retaining about 96% of always-long performance. It further provides a cost-quality trade-off on $R^2$-AVSBench without target-label tuning, rather than an accuracy improvement over always-long. Error analysis links harmful long reasoning to phrase and localization drift, illustrating the benefit of bypassing unnecessary reasoning on simple queries. Ultimately, our results support efficient adaptive reasoning in Ref-AVS through pre-decisional internal representations.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 35 pages, 7 figures

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: UniMore: Fine-Grained Supervision for Unified Understanding and Generation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Unified multimodal models combine image understanding and generation within one system, creating an opportunity to improve both capabilities through paired image--text supervision. We examine the outputs of a pretrained unified model in both directions and observe a loss of specificity: generated images can contain the requested objects with incorrect attributes, while captions identify a scene without expressing its distinguishing details. These failures call for supervision that specifies both the visual content to realize and the descriptive differences to distinguish. We propose UniMore, a post-training method that derives these complementary learning tasks from the fine-grained content of image--text pairs. The generation route predicts grounded crops from their corresponding phrases, matching the scope of the condition and visual target while using the native visual objective. The understanding route combines positive-caption fitting with ranking against captions that omit or alter details, conditioned on the full image. The two routes are optimized independently, and their learned updates are combined into a single unified model without changing its inference procedure. Experiments show gains across multiple understanding and generation benchmarks.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Refer-CityFlow and M3Track: A Benchmark Dataset and Reference Framework for Language-Driven Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Referring multi-object tracking enables users to specify targets through natural language, but existing Refer-MOT benchmarks primarily focus on single-camera settings. We formalize Referring Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking (Refer-MTMCT), where free-form queries specify identity-consistent trajectories to be recovered across a network of sequential, sparse-overlap cameras. We introduce Refer-CityFlow, a benchmark built on CityFlow's global cross-camera identity annotations and augmented with language queries requiring joint language grounding, cross-camera association, and spatio-temporal reasoning. Refer-CityFlow covers 96 videos from 40 roadside cameras with 660+ identity-consistent cross-camera trajectories, 4,362 trajectory-level descriptions, and 7,699 queries, including 1,699 real-user queries collected from 50 participants. Reference experiments on the four-camera Scenario 02 show that single-camera referring trackers reach 14.95-18.28 HOTA on real-user queries, while the evaluated cross-view method achieves about 0.05 HOTA in direct transfer. To establish reference performance, we provide M3Track, a modular multimodal reference framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent orchestrates interchangeable detection, tracking, and cross-camera association modules. M3Track reaches 44.10 HOTA and 65.40 IDF1 on the same real-user query set. The project repository is available at https://github.com/phuongnguyen194/Refer-CityFlow-and--M3Track.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted for publication at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027), Evaluations and Datasets Track. 10 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: When does the head leave? Shared timing and a movement clock in 360-degree video viewing
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: A $360^\circ$ streaming system only needs high quality where the viewer faces, so knowing when a head will turn away matters as much as where it will go. Across four public head-tracking datasets, two used to fix and validate the method and two held out for testing, three patterns emerge on the held-out sets. First, viewers facing the same region turn away within a second of one another far more often than time-shifted traces allow. That estimate is about five times the pairwise threshold for a video timing one departure in ten, mapping to roughly one and a third to over twice that one-in-ten share. The excess co-departing fraction is 0.0422, with a 90% interval from 0.0279 to 0.0565. Second, time since the last large head movement improves held-out departure prediction beyond video and viewer effects. It adds 0.0793 nats per departure, a predictive dependence rather than proof of an internal timer. Third, on the eye-tracked test set, gaze crosses the region boundary after the head starts moving, lagging head onset by 0.30 s. Because headsets record continuous angles, a departure exists only after a rule marks when a settled hold ends once the head swings past a speed and angle threshold. Before touching the test sets, we picked one primary setting for the headline estimates above and tested 18 settings on synthetic traces with planted answers, requiring at least nine passing settings for robustness. Fifteen settings passed for the clock and all 15 valid settings confirm its gain; 8 passed for synchrony and all 8 valid settings agree, one short of the nine-setting bar; and 6 of 7 dual-validated settings agree on gaze lag. Synchrony validation drops from 17 or 18 passing settings under guessed noise to 8 under measured noise because zero-tolerance rules reject a small baseline offset, consistently positive at one dataset size, as datasets grow.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 10 pages, 1 table. v3: Complete empirical rebuild across four public 360-degree head- and eye-tracking datasets (two calibration, two held-out test sets), adding whole-trace shift synchrony testing, discrete-time movement-clock hazard modeling, and synthetic detector validation across an 18-setting grid

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Structural and Representational Agency in LLM-Driven Timbre Generation and Interpolation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Generative creative interfaces routinely report the user's position within a space of possibilities. Such displays imply that the quantities shown were measured from the artefact; in a growing class of systems they are instead predicted by a language model describing its own output, and the two are indistinguishable on screen. Most creative domains lack an agreed measurement against which such a self-report can be checked; audio admits one. In a measurement study of a working LLM-driven timbre interface, what a user can cause proves separable from what the interface reports. The first is exactly characterisable: the reachable set is a zonotope in parameter space whose dimension increases by one per sound placed, so the space the model may act within is demonstrably the user's own. The second is inaccurate. The displayed position differs from measurement by approximately three times the width of that region, and the error has two independent sources: model-predicted coordinates, whose accuracy varies twofold between the two models evaluated, and the interpolation step, which arises from combining synthesiser parameters and is unaffected by model quality. End to end, 27 of 36 refinement instructions produced no perceptible change, and under the weaker model the facility performed no action while reporting convergence. Effective agency (what a user can cause) and epistemic agency (whether they can know it) are therefore separable and independently engineered: structurally enforced constraints survive model failure, whereas guarantees resting on the model's own report do not. The failure mode that remains is silence presented as success. We close with a short protocol for building and auditing such displays.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 11 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Conference, Creative AI Track)

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Streaming Persistent 3D Gaussian Proxies for View-Flexible Remote Rendering
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Cloud rendering executes demanding real-time graphics on a remote server, but conventional video transmission constrains the displayed image to the server-rendered viewpoint. Image-space warping can compensate for client motion during transport and display latency, although its accuracy decreases with pose offset. We investigate an alternative approach in which the server constructs a persistent, client-renderable 3D Gaussian proxy online from game-engine render buffers and progressively transmits independently renderable spatial tiles. Our Unity prototype supports continuous optimization and expansion, approximate relighting, and engine-tracked rigid-object motion, while the client renders locally from its current viewpoint. We evaluate four scenes under controlled pose offsets and encoded walkthroughs, comparing the proxy with stale server-rendered frames, depth-assisted warping using HEVC with one, three, or five reference views. The proxy maintains stable quality as pose offset increases. At 50 Mbit/s, it achieves higher SSIM than all evaluated warping configurations at 367 ms on all four scenes and at 183 ms on three of the four scenes. The results identify complementary operating regimes: image warping is effective at small pose offsets, conventional video is rate-efficient when only the server-rendered viewpoint is required, while the persistent proxy provides robust viewpoint flexibility when the original renderer cannot be executed at the client.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Recent advances in Gaussian splatting have enabled efficient and photorealistic head avatar reconstruction, yet monocular video-based or image-based methods still suffer from under-constrained geometry and texture, leading to artifacts such as blurring, stretching, and temporal instability. We present EDGAR (Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement), a conditional diffusion framework designed to enhance the quality of Gaussian avatars by correcting artifacts while preserving identity fidelity. To train EDGAR, we construct EDGAR-SET, a hybrid triplet dataset composed of real-captured and synthetic-rendered samples, which simulates realistic Gaussian avatar failure cases by pairing degraded renderings with ground-truth and reference images. EDGAR refines degraded frames through a fusion block that injects identity features extracted by the self-supervised Sapiens model into a one-step diffusion backbone, enabling effective artifact removal without sacrificing efficiency. Our EDGAR model incorporates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture to address diverse degradation types and severity levels. The refined multi-view renderings are subsequently used as pseudo-targets to optimize a single underlying Gaussian avatar, so that the final avatar can be rendered without applying EDGAR to every output frame. Experiments on three different Gaussian avatar reconstruction methods, each evaluated under three different settings, show improvements in both perceptual and reconstruction measures over the raw outputs and an SDEdit-style refinement baseline. In addition, cross-view evaluation demonstrates improved calibrated consistency, while tests under large yaw and open-mouth expressions verify robustness under extreme settings. These results collectively indicate a useful operating regime for recoverable appearance artifacts. The code is available at https://kwanyun.github.io/edgar/
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted to ACM Transactions on Graphics

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: TV-AudioRemover: Joint Text-Visual Guided Sound Removal with Multi-Task Hard-Mixture Curriculum
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Visual object removal can eliminate a target from video frames, yet its acoustic trace persists in the soundtrack, causing obvious audio-visual inconsistency. Existing video inpainting models operate solely on pixels, while audio editing models, especially for the sound removal task, are typically driven by text and therefore rely on limited single-modal control, which is less effective than multimodal guidance that provides stronger semantic grounding and temporal synchronization cues. In this paper, we present Text-Visual Guided Sound Removal (TV-AudioRemover), a target sound removal framework that leverages the visually edited video together with a natural-language instruction to suppress the sound associated with the removed visual object from the original audio mixture. To acquire high-quality training data, we devise a pipeline to construct a million-scale dataset of single-object audio-visual aligned samples, from which we synthesize mixture-target pairs customized for model training. To effectively leverage visual context and follow instruction intent, we augment the model architecture with task tokens, generalizable instruction modeling, and modality-specific global guidance. We further adopt multi-task training to strengthen task-role comprehension, and employ a hard-mixture curriculum that leverages semantically similar acoustic mixtures during fine-tuning to enhance fine-grained source discrimination. To support evaluation, we present AV-Remove-Bench, a comprehensive audio-visual object removal benchmark, along with dedicated objective metrics and an MLLM-based evaluation protocol. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both subjective and objective metrics. Project page: https://yjx-research.github.io/TV-AudioRemover/.
